title.zh: 卷24 燕鳳 許謙 張衮 崔玄伯 鄧淵
title.en: Volume 24: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, Deng Yuan
title.raw: 卷24 燕鳳 許謙 張衮 崔玄伯 鄧淵 Volume 24: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, Deng Yuan

sentences.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 張袞 崔玄伯 鄧淵

translations.literal: Yan Feng; Xu Qian; Zhang Gun; Cui Xuanbo; Deng Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, and Deng Yuan

sentences.zh: 燕鳳，字子章，代人也。

translations.literal: Yan Feng, styled Zizhang, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Feng, whose style was Zizhang, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 好學，博綜經史，明習陰陽讖緯。

translations.literal: He loved learning, mastered the classics and histories in breadth, and was skilled in yin-yang omens and weft-text prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar, he ranged widely through the classics and histories and was versed in yin-yang lore and prophetic weft-texts.

sentences.zh: 昭成素聞其名，使人以禮迎致之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng had long heard his name and sent men to welcome him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng, who had long known his reputation, sent envoys to receive him with full ritual honors.

sentences.zh: 鳳不應聘。

translations.literal: Feng would not accept the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Feng refused to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 乃命諸軍圍代城，謂城人曰：「燕鳳不來，吾將屠汝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the armies to besiege Dai city and said to the townspeople: "If Yan Feng does not come, I shall slaughter you all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng then had his forces surround Dai and told the inhabitants: "Unless Yan Feng comes, I will put every one of you to the sword.

sentences.zh: 」代人懼，送鳳。

translations.literal: " The men of Dai were afraid and sent Feng forth.
translations.idiomatic: " Terrified, the people of Dai sent Feng out to him.

sentences.zh: 昭成與語，大悅，待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng spoke with him and was greatly pleased, treating him with the rites due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng talked with him at length, took great delight in him, and honored him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 後拜代王左長史，參決國事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Left Chief Clerk to the Prince of Dai and took part in deciding state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Left Chief Clerk to the Prince of Dai and joined in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 又以經授獻明帝。

translations.literal: He also taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

sentences.zh: 苻堅遣使牛恬朝貢。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent the envoy Niu Tian with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian dispatched the envoy Niu Tian to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 令鳳報之。

translations.literal: He ordered Feng to reply on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng charged Feng to answer in his name.

sentences.zh: 堅問鳳：「代王何如人？

translations.literal: Jian asked Feng: "What sort of man is the Prince of Dai?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian asked Feng: "What manner of ruler is the Prince of Dai?

sentences.zh: 」鳳對曰：「寬和仁愛，經略高遠，一時之雄主，常有并吞天下之志。

translations.literal: " Feng answered: "Broad and harmonious, benevolent and loving, lofty in strategy and far-reaching in design—a hero of his age, who ever harbors the will to swallow the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng replied: "Mild and humane, far-sighted in counsel—a champion of the hour who constantly dreams of uniting the world under his rule.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「卿輩北人，無鋼甲利器，敵弱則進，強即退走，安能并兼？

translations.literal: " Jian said: "You northerners lack steel armor and sharp weapons; when the foe is weak you advance, when he is strong you flee at once—how could you annex and combine?
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian said: "You northerners have no plate mail or keen blades; you press forward only against the weak and run when the strong appear—how could you ever conquer all?

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「北人壯悍，上馬持三仗，驅馳若飛。

translations.literal: " Feng said: "Northerners are stalwart and fierce; mounted, each man bears three weapons and charges like the wind.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng said: "The north breeds hard men; in the saddle each warrior carries three arms and flies across the plain.

sentences.zh: 主上雄雋，率服北土，控弦百萬，號令若一。

translations.literal: Our lord is heroic and outstanding; he has made the northern lands submit, commands a million bowstrings, and his orders run as one.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is brilliant and bold; the north obeys him, a million bowmen answer his call, and his word is law to every camp.

sentences.zh: 軍無輜重樵爨之苦，輕行速捷，因敵取資。

translations.literal: The army knows none of the hardship of baggage trains or cooking fires; it moves light and strikes fast, taking supplies from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: His host marches without the drag of wagons or camp kitchens; light and swift, it lives off what it seizes from the foe.

sentences.zh: 此南方所以疲弊，而北方之所常勝也。

translations.literal: This is why the south grows weary and broken while the north wins again and again.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the south wears itself down while the north wins battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「彼國人馬，實為多少？

translations.literal: " Jian said: "How many men and horses does that state truly have?
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian asked: "How many fighting men and horses does Dai really field?

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「控弦之士數十萬，馬百萬匹。

translations.literal: " Feng said: "Bowmen number in the hundreds of thousands; horses, a million head.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng answered: "Archers in the hundreds of thousands; horses by the million.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「卿言人眾可爾，說馬太多，是虛辭耳。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "What you say of men may pass; speaking of so many horses is empty boasting.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian said: "Your count of men I can credit; a million horses is mere brag.

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「雲中川自東山至西河二百里，北山至南山百有餘里，每歲孟秋，馬常大集，略為滿川。

translations.literal: " Feng said: "From East Mountain to West River the Yunzhong valley runs two hundred li; from North Mountain to South Mountain it is more than a hundred li. Every year in early autumn the horses gather in vast herds and nearly fill the river valley.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng said: "East Mountain to West River along the Yunzhong is two hundred li; north to south, more than a hundred. Each early autumn the herds assemble until the valley is all but covered with horses.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，使人之言，猶當未盡。

translations.literal: Judging from this, what your envoy reports still falls short of the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Judge by that, and even your messenger's tale understates the case.

sentences.zh: 」鳳還，堅厚加贈遺。

translations.literal: " When Feng returned, Jian heaped gifts upon him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Feng went home, Fu Jian loaded him with presents.

sentences.zh: 及昭成崩，太祖將遷長安。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng died, Taizu was about to move to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death, Taizu was preparing to relocate to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 鳳以太祖幼弱，固請於苻堅曰：「代主初崩，臣子亡叛，遺孫沖幼，莫相輔立。

translations.literal: Feng, because Taizu was young and weak, firmly petitioned Fu Jian, saying: "The Prince of Dai has just died; his ministers have scattered in rebellion; the orphan heir is still a child and no one stands to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the heir still a child, Feng pressed Fu Jian: "The Prince of Dai is newly dead; his officers have fled or turned traitor; the grandson left behind is an infant with no one to raise him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其別部大人劉庫仁勇而有智，鐵弗衞辰狡猾多變，皆不可獨任。

translations.literal: The tribal grandee Liu Kuren is brave and wise; the Tiefu chieftain Weichen is crafty and changeable—neither may be trusted alone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren of the separate tribes is bold and shrewd; the Tiefu leader Weichen is sly and shifting—neither should hold power alone.

sentences.zh: 宜分諸部為二，令此兩人統之。

translations.literal: You should divide the tribes in two and let these two men command them.
translations.idiomatic: Split the tribal following between them and set each to command his half.

sentences.zh: 兩人素有深讎，其勢莫敢先發。

translations.literal: The two have long borne a deep feud; neither will dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: They have hated each other for years; neither will dare move before the other.

sentences.zh: 此禦邊之良策。

translations.literal: This is a fine stratagem for guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That is the soundest way to secure the border.

sentences.zh: 待其孫長，乃存而立之，是陛下施大惠於亡國也。

translations.literal: Wait until the grandson has grown, then preserve the state and set him up—this would be Your Majesty's great grace to a fallen kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy comes of age, restore the realm and enthrone him—Your Majesty would then show supreme mercy to a ruined house.

sentences.zh: 」堅從之。

translations.literal: " Jian followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 鳳尋東還。

translations.literal: Feng soon returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Feng soon made his way back east.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，歷吏部郎、給事黃門侍郎、行臺尚書，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he served in succession as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Acting Director of the Palace Secretariat, and was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu's accession he rose through Director of Personnel, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Acting Director of the Secretariat, and was held in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，與崔玄伯、封懿、梁越等入講經傳，出議朝政。

translations.literal: In Taizong's reign he joined Cui Xuanbo, Feng Yi, Liang Yue, and others in lecturing on the classics and in deliberating court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he sat with Cui Xuanbo, Feng Yi, Liang Yue, and others to expound the classics and debate affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，以舊勳賜爵平舒侯，加鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu's reign, for old merit he was granted the title Marquis of Pingshu and made General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu began his reign, Feng received the marquisate of Pingshu and the rank General Who Pacifies the Distance for long service.

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Shenlu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shenlu year 1.

sentences.zh: 子才，襲。

translations.literal: His son Cai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、平遠將軍。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子元孫，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yuansun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansun took the succession.

sentences.zh: 官至博陵太守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died without further office.

sentences.zh: 子世宗，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shizong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 許謙，字元遜，代人也。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, styled Yuansun, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, whose style was Yuansun, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有文才，善天文圖讖之學。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary talent and was skilled in astronomy, charts, and weft-text prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed literary gifts and mastered astronomy, star-charts, and prophetic weft-texts.

sentences.zh: 建國時，將家歸附，昭成嘉之，擢為代王郎中令，兼掌文記。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he brought his household to submit; Zhaocheng commended this and promoted him to Director of Gentlemen for the Prince of Dai, with charge also of written records.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was founded he came in with his clan; Zhaocheng praised him, made him Director of Gentlemen to the Prince of Dai, and put him in charge of the archives.

sentences.zh: 與燕鳳俱授獻明帝經。

translations.literal: Together with Yan Feng he taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan Feng together instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

sentences.zh: 從征衞辰，以功賜僮隸三十戶。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Weichen he was rewarded with thirty households of bondsmen for merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the expedition against Weichen he earned thirty households of retainers as a reward for service.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩後，謙徙長安。

translations.literal: After Zhaocheng died, Qian moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death, Qian went to live at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 苻堅從弟行唐公洛鎮和龍，請謙之鎮。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang, Luo, held Helong and invited Qian to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's cousin Fu Luo, Duke of Xingtang, who governed Helong, asked Qian to join him there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以繼母老辭還。

translations.literal: Before long, citing his stepmother's age, he asked leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, pleading his stepmother's advanced years, he sought leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 登國初，遂歸太祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he returned to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengguo was proclaimed he came back to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖悅，以為右司馬，與張袞等參贊初基。

translations.literal: Taizu was pleased and made him Right Major of Horse, and with Zhang Gun and others he helped lay the first foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu welcomed him, named him Right Major of Horse, and with Zhang Gun and others he helped build the new order.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶來寇也，太祖使謙告難於姚興。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came raiding, Taizu sent Qian to report the crisis to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Taizu dispatched Qian to tell Yao Xing of the peril.

sentences.zh: 興遣將楊佛嵩率眾來援，而佛嵩稽緩。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong with troops to aid, but Fosong dragged his feet.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent General Yang Fosong with an army, but Fosong moved slowly.

sentences.zh: 太祖命謙為書以遺佛嵩曰：「夫杖順以翦遺，乘義而攻昧，未有非其運而顯功，無其時而著業。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Qian to write a letter and send it to Fosong, saying: "To lean on Heaven's mandate in cutting off the doomed, to ride righteousness in striking the benighted—never has merit shone without its season, nor achievement stood without its hour.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had Qian draft a letter to Fosong: "To wield the Mandate against a house already failing, to strike in the name of justice against a blinded foe—no triumph ever shone outside its season, no deed ever stood outside its time.

sentences.zh: 慕容無道，侵我疆埸，師老兵疲，天亡期至，是以遣使命軍，必望克赴。

translations.literal: Murong is without the Way; he violates our borders; his troops are old and weary; Heaven's hour of his fall has come—therefore I send this mission and army, and surely look for swift arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao is lawless; he tramples our marches; his soldiers are spent; the day of his ruin is at hand—hence this embassy and this host, and I expect you without delay.

sentences.zh: 將軍據方邵之任，總熊虎之師，事與機會，今其時也。

translations.literal: General, you hold the charge of a border province and command troops fierce as bears and tigers; the matter meets its moment—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a frontier command and lead warriors fierce as bear and tiger; fortune offers itself—this is the hour.

sentences.zh: 因此而舉，役不再駕，千載之勳，一朝可立。

translations.literal: If you strike on this basis, the campaign need not be fought twice; merit for a thousand years may be raised in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now and the war need not be fought twice; glory to last a millennium can be won before noon.

sentences.zh: 然後高會雲中，進師三魏，舉觴稱壽，不亦綽乎。

translations.literal: Then hold high council in Yunzhong, advance the army into the Three Weis, raise the cup and toast long life—is that not magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: Then feast in Yunzhong, march into the Three Weis, lift the wine and toast long life—would that not be splendid?

sentences.zh: 」佛嵩乃倍道兼行。

translations.literal: " Fosong thereupon marched day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " Fosong doubled his pace and raced to the field.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，賜謙爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and granted Qian the title Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 重遣謙與佛嵩盟曰：「昔殷湯有鳴條之誓，周武有河陽之盟，所以藉神靈，昭忠信，夫親仁善隣，古之令軌，歃血割牲，以敦永穆。

translations.literal: He again sent Qian to ally with Fosong, saying: "Of old Tang of Yin swore at Mingtiao and Wu of Zhou at Heyang—they called on the spirits to make loyalty and faith shine forth. To cherish the humane and be good to neighbors is the ancient standard; they drank blood and cut the victim to seal lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qian again to swear alliance with Fosong: "Tang of Yin bound himself at Mingtiao, King Wu of Zhou at Heyang—each invoked the spirits to witness faith. To love the humane and treat neighbors well is the ancient rule; blood was drunk and the victim cut to seal peace forever.

sentences.zh: 今既盟之後，言歸其好，分災恤患，休戚是同。

translations.literal: Now that we have sworn, let words return to goodwill; let us share disaster and relieve distress, sharing joy and sorrow as one.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are allied, let us speak only friendship; share each other's calamity, ease each other's grief, and make our weal and woe one.

sentences.zh: 有違此盟，神祗斯殛。

translations.literal: Whoever breaks this pact, let the spirits destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this oath, let the gods strike him dead.

sentences.zh: 」寶敗，佛嵩乃還。

translations.literal: " When Bao was defeated, Fosong returned.
translations.idiomatic: " When Bao fell, Fosong marched home.

sentences.zh: 明年，慕容垂復來寇。

translations.literal: The next year Murong Chui came raiding again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Murong Chui invaded again.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂謙曰：「今事急矣，非卿豈能復致姚師，卿其行也。

translations.literal: Taizu said to Qian: "The matter is urgent now; without you, who could again bring Yao's army? Go.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Qian: "Affairs are desperate; only you could summon Yao's host again—set out at once.

sentences.zh: 」謙未發而垂退，乃止。

translations.literal: " Qian had not yet departed when Chui withdrew, and the mission was halted.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian had not yet left when Chui retreated, and the errand was called off.

sentences.zh: 及聞垂死，謙上書勸進。

translations.literal: When he heard that Chui had died, Qian submitted a memorial urging Taizu to take the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Chui's death, Qian memorialized urging Taizu to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: Taizu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was pleased with the counsel.

sentences.zh: 并州平，以謙為陽曲護軍，賜爵平舒侯、安遠將軍。

translations.literal: When Bing province was pacified, Qian was made Protector of Yangqu and granted the title Marquis of Pingshu and the rank General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: After Bing was pacified he was named Protector of Yangqu, Marquis of Pingshu, and General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 皇始元年卒官，時年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in office in the first year of Huangshi, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Huangshi year 1, at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、左光祿大夫、幽州刺史、高陽公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, Inspector of Youzhou, and Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, Inspector of Youzhou, and Duke of Gaoyang, with the temple name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子洛陽，襲。

translations.literal: His son Luoyang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoyang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容寶，為冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Murong Bao he served as Champion Major.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Murong Bao he was Champion Major.

sentences.zh: 後為祁令。

translations.literal: Later he was made Magistrate of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He later became magistrate of Qi county.

sentences.zh: 太宗追錄謙功，以洛陽為雁門太守。

translations.literal: Taizong, recalling Qian's merit, made Luoyang Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, honoring Qian's service, appointed Luoyang Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 洛陽家田三生嘉禾，皆異壟合穎，世祖善之。

translations.literal: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of auspicious grain grew, each with strange ridges and joined ears; Emperor Shizu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Three stalks of lucky grain sprang on Luoyang's land, each with unusual furrows and fused ears; Emperor Shizu approved.

sentences.zh: 進爵北地公，加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: His rank was raised to Duke of Beidi and he was made General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Beidi and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 出為明壘鎮將，居八年，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as garrison commander of Minglei and, after eight years in post, died.
translations.idiomatic: He served eight years as garrison commander of Minglei, then died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子寄生，襲爵，降為侯。

translations.literal: His son Jisheng inherited the title, which was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited, but the rank was lowered to marquis.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huangxing year 1.

sentences.zh: 洛陽弟安國，中山太守。

translations.literal: Luoyang's younger brother Anguo was Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's brother Anguo became Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 安國弟安都，廣寧、滄水二郡太守。

translations.literal: Anguo's younger brother Andu was Administrator of the two commanderies of Guangning and Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo's brother Andu governed Guangning and Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 加揚威將軍。

translations.literal: He was further made General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 賜爵東光子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: He received the viscounty of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 天安初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Tian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Tian'an era.

sentences.zh: 贈平遠將軍、冀州刺史、東光侯，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance, Inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, with the posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was General Who Pacifies the Distance, Inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, temple name Lie.

sentences.zh: 子白虎，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Baihu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baihu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 為侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was Attendant Censor-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Censor-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後以罪免官，奪爵。

translations.literal: Later, for crime he was removed from office and stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: Later, convicted of an offense, he was dismissed and deprived of his rank.

sentences.zh: 許謙，字元遜，代人也。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, styled Yuansun, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, whose style was Yuansun, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有文才，善天文圖讖之學。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary talent and was skilled in astronomy, charts, and weft-text prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed literary gifts and mastered astronomy, star-charts, and prophetic weft-texts.

sentences.zh: 建國時，將家歸附，昭成嘉之，擢為代王郎中令，兼掌文記。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he brought his household to submit; Zhaocheng commended this and promoted him to Director of Gentlemen for the Prince of Dai, with charge also of written records.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was founded he came in with his clan; Zhaocheng praised him, made him Director of Gentlemen to the Prince of Dai, and put him in charge of the archives.

sentences.zh: 與燕鳳俱授獻明帝經。

translations.literal: Together with Yan Feng he taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan Feng together instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

sentences.zh: 從征衞辰，以功賜僮隸三十戶。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Weichen he was rewarded with thirty households of bondsmen for merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the expedition against Weichen he earned thirty households of retainers as a reward for service.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩後，謙徙長安。

translations.literal: After Zhaocheng died, Qian moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaocheng's death, Qian went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 苻堅從弟行唐公洛鎮和龍，請謙之鎮。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang Luo, held Helong and requested Qian to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's younger cousin Luo, Duke of Xingtang, held Helong and asked Qian to take command there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以繼母老辭還。

translations.literal: Before long, he pleaded to return because his stepmother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked leave to return, citing his stepmother's age.

sentences.zh: 登國初，遂歸太祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Denguo, he returned to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Denguo era he came back to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖悅，以為右司馬，與張袞等參贊初基。

translations.literal: Taizu was pleased and made him Right Marshal; with Zhang Gun and others he assisted in laying the foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was pleased, made him Right Marshal, and with Zhang Gun and others helped build the new order.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶來寇也，太祖使謙告難於姚興。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Taizu sent Qian to report the crisis to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Taizu sent Qian to ask Yao Xing for aid.

sentences.zh: 興遣將楊佛嵩率眾來援，而佛嵩稽緩。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong to lead troops in relief, but Fosong was dilatory.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sent Yang Fosong with an army, but Fosong dragged his feet.

sentences.zh: 太祖命謙為書以遺佛嵩曰：「夫杖順以翦遺，乘義而攻昧，未有非其運而顯功，無其時而著業。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Qian to write a letter to send to Fosong, saying: "To wield legitimacy in cutting off the remnant, to ride righteousness in attacking the benighted — none has displayed achievement outside his destined turn, or established enterprise without its season.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had Qian write to Fosong: "To strike the doomed in the name of order and attack the blind in the name of right — no one wins glory against the times or builds lasting fame out of season."

sentences.zh: 慕容無道，侵我疆埸，師老兵疲，天亡期至，是以遣使命軍，必望克赴。

translations.literal: Murong Bao is without the Way, encroaching on our borders; his army is old and weary, the day of Heaven's destruction is at hand — therefore I send envoys and troops, surely expecting you can arrive in time to strike.
translations.idiomatic: "Murong Bao is lawless and trespasses on our borders; his soldiers are spent and Heaven's judgment is due — I send envoys and an army and count on you to come in time."

sentences.zh: 將軍據方邵之任，總熊虎之師，事與機會，今其時也。

translations.literal: General, you hold charge of a border province, commanding troops fierce as bear and tiger; the affair matches its moment — now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: "You hold a frontier command and lead troops like bears and tigers; the moment fits — now is the hour."

sentences.zh: 因此而舉，役不再駕，千載之勳，一朝可立。

translations.literal: If you strike on this basis, the campaign need not be mounted twice; merit for a thousand years can be established in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: "Strike now and the war need not be fought twice; glory for a thousand years can be won in one morning."

sentences.zh: 然後高會雲中，進師三魏，舉觴稱壽，不亦綽乎。

translations.literal: Then you can feast grandly in Yunzhong, advance your army through the three Wei regions, raise your cup and wish long life — is that not ample scope?"
translations.idiomatic: "Then feast in Yunzhong, march through the three Weis, raise your cup to long life — what could be grander?"

sentences.zh: 」佛嵩乃倍道兼行。

translations.literal: " Fosong then marched by double stages.
translations.idiomatic: Fosong then forced a double march.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，賜謙爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and granted Qian the enfeoffment Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 重遣謙與佛嵩盟曰：「昔殷湯有鳴條之誓，周武有河陽之盟，所以藉神靈，昭忠信，夫親仁善隣，古之令軌，歃血割牲，以敦永穆。

translations.literal: He again sent Qian to ally with Fosong in oath, saying: "In old times Tang of Yin had the oath of Mingtiao, Wu of Zhou the covenant of Heyang — by these they borrowed divine power and displayed loyalty and trustworthiness. To be intimate with the benevolent and good to neighbors is the ancient perfect standard; blood-oath and cutting sacrificial victims are to deepen eternal peace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qian again to swear alliance with Fosong: "Tang of Yin swore at Mingtiao and Wu of Zhou at Heyang to borrow the gods' witness and bind faith. To cherish the humane and be good to neighbors is the ancient model; blood-oath and sacrifice seal peace forever."

sentences.zh: 今既盟之後，言歸其好，分災恤患，休戚是同。

translations.literal: Now after we have sworn alliance, let words return to amity; divide disasters and pity calamities — weal and woe are one.
translations.idiomatic: "After this oath let us keep amity, share disaster and pity each other's woes — one fortune, one fate."

sentences.zh: 有違此盟，神祗斯殛。

translations.literal: Whoever violates this alliance — the spirits destroy him."
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever breaks this pact — let the spirits destroy him."

sentences.zh: 」寶敗，佛嵩乃還。

translations.literal: " Bao was defeated and Fosong then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was beaten and Fosong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，慕容垂復來寇。

translations.literal: The next year Murong Chui again came to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Murong Chui invaded again.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂謙曰：「今事急矣，非卿豈能復致姚師，卿其行也。

translations.literal: Taizu said to Qian: "Matters are desperate now; apart from you, who could again bring Yao's army? You must go."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Qian, "The crisis is acute; who but you could summon Yao's troops again? Go at once."

sentences.zh: 」謙未發而垂退，乃止。

translations.literal: " Before Qian set out Chui withdrew, so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Before Qian departed, Chui had already retreated, so the mission was called off.

sentences.zh: 及聞垂死，謙上書勸進。

translations.literal: When he heard Chui had died, Qian submitted a memorial urging advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Chui was dead, Qian memorialized urging Taizu to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: Taizu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved.

sentences.zh: 并州平，以謙為陽曲護軍，賜爵平舒侯、安遠將軍。

translations.literal: When Bing province was pacified, Qian was made Protector of Yangqu, granted the enfeoffments Marquis of Pingshu and General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingzhou was pacified, Qian became Protector of Yangqu and was made Marquis of Pingshu and General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 皇始元年卒官，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In Huangshi year 1 he died in office at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangshi year 1 he died in office at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、左光祿大夫、幽州刺史、高陽公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of the Left, Inspector of Youzhou, Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of the Left, Youzhou inspector, Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子洛陽，襲。

translations.literal: His son Luoyang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoyang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容寶，為冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: On campaign against Murong Bao he was Champion Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Murong Bao he served as champion marshal.

sentences.zh: 後為祁令。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was magistrate of Qi — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太宗追錄謙功，以洛陽為雁門太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong recorded Qian's merit and made Luoyang Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong recalled Qian's service and made Luoyang administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 洛陽家田三生嘉禾，皆異壟合穎，世祖善之。

translations.literal: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of auspicious grain grew, each on separate ridges joined in one ear — Shizu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of auspicious grain grew on separate ridges but with ears joined as one; Shizu was pleased.

sentences.zh: 進爵北地公，加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Advanced to Duke of Beidi and General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Beidi and General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 出為明壘鎮將，居八年，卒。

translations.literal: Sent out as commanding general of Ming Lei and dwelt there eight years, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as commanding general of Ming Lei, held the post eight years, and died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子寄生，襲爵，降為侯。

translations.literal: His son Jisheng inherited the rank, demoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited, but the title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年卒。

translations.literal: In Huangxing year 1 he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing year 1 he died — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 洛陽弟安國，中山太守。

translations.literal: Luoyang's younger brother Anguo was Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's younger brother Anguo was administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 安國弟安都，廣寧、滄水二郡太守。

translations.literal: Anguo's younger brother Andu was Administrator of Guangning and Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo's younger brother Andu was administrator of Guangning and Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 加揚威將軍。

translations.literal: Also made General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 賜爵東光子。

translations.literal: Granted the enfeoffment Son of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Son of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 天安初卒。

translations.literal: In Tian'an year 1 he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Tian'an year 1 he died — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 贈平遠將軍、冀州刺史、東光侯，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of Jizhou, Marquis of Dongguang, posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Jizhou inspector, Marquis of Dongguang, posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 子白虎，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Baihu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baihu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 為侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was attendant-in-ordinary in the Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was attendant-in-ordinary in the Personal Guard — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 後以罪免官，奪爵。

translations.literal: Later for crime he was removed from office and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for a crime, he was dismissed and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 張袞，字洪龍，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, came from Juyang in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖翼，遼東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi had been administrator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父卓，昌黎太守。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo was Administrator of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo was administrator of Changli.

sentences.zh: 袞初為郡五官掾，純厚篤實，好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Gun at first was the commandery Registrar of Five Offices — pure, thick, and sincere, loving learning, with literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gun began as the commandery registrar of five offices — honest, steady, studious, and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 太祖為代王，選為左長史。

translations.literal: When Taizu was Prince of Dai he was chosen as Left Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as left chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 從太祖征蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu on campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕遁走，追之五六百里。

translations.literal: The Rouran fled; they pursued them five or six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fled and the army pursued five or six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 諸部帥因袞言於太祖曰：「今賊遠糧盡，不宜深入，請速還軍。

translations.literal: The tribal chiefs spoke through Gun to Taizu, saying: "Now the enemy is far and grain is spent; we should not press deep — please turn the army back quickly."
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs spoke through Gun to Taizu: "The foe is far and our grain is gone; do not go deeper — turn back at once."

sentences.zh: 」太祖令袞問諸部帥，若殺副馬，足三日食否。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Gun to ask the tribal chiefs whether, if they slaughtered spare horses, there would be food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Gun to ask the chiefs whether killing the remount horses would feed the army three days.

sentences.zh: 皆言足也。

translations.literal: All said it would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: All said it would.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃倍道追之，及於廣漠赤地南床山下，大破之。

translations.literal: Taizu then pressed the pursuit at double speed and overtook them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then doubled the pace, caught them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 既而太祖問袞：「卿曹外人知我前問三日糧意乎？

translations.literal: Afterward Taizu asked Gun: "Do people outside our circle know the meaning of my earlier question about three days' grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu asked Gun, "Do outsiders know why I asked about three days' grain?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「皆莫知也。

translations.literal: He answered: "None know."
translations.idiomatic: Gun answered, "No one does."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「此易知耳。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "This is easy to know.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "It is simple.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕奔走數日，畜產之餘，至水必留。

translations.literal: The Rouran had fled for days; after their livestock's leavings, whenever they reached water they were sure to halt.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rouran had run for days; after their herds' leavings they must halt at every water."

sentences.zh: 計其道程，三日足及。

translations.literal: Calculating their route, three days would be enough to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: "Count their route and three days suffice to catch them."

sentences.zh: 輕騎卒至，出其不意，彼必驚散，其勢然矣。

translations.literal: Light cavalry arriving suddenly would take them unawares; they would scatter in alarm — such is the logic."
translations.idiomatic: "Light horse arriving suddenly will startle them into flight — that is the logic."

sentences.zh: 」袞以太祖言出告部帥，咸曰：「聖策長遠，非愚近所及也。」

translations.literal: Gun took Taizu's words out and told the tribal chiefs; all said: "The sage's plan reaches far — it is not what the near-sighted can match."
translations.idiomatic: Gun repeated Taizu's words to the chiefs; all said, "The sage's design reaches far beyond what short sight can grasp."

sentences.zh: 袞常參大謀，決策幃幄，太祖器之，禮遇優厚。

translations.literal: Gun constantly took part in great plans, deciding policy within the curtain; Taizu valued him and treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was constantly in counsel at the heart of strategy; Taizu prized him and honored him generously.

sentences.zh: 袞每告人曰：「昔樂毅杖策於燕昭，公達委身於魏武，[1]蓋命世難可期，千載不易遇。

translations.literal: Gun often told others: "In old times Yue Yi leaned on his staff for Yan Zhao, and Xun Yu devoted himself to Cao Cao;[1] a match for the age is hard to await, and a meeting once in a thousand years is not easily met.
translations.idiomatic: Gun often said to others, "Yue Yi served Yan Zhao with his staff and Xun Yu gave himself to Cao Cao;[1] a lord for the age is rare, and a once-in-a-millennium chance is rarer still."

sentences.zh: 主上天姿傑邁，逸志凌霄，必能囊括六合，混一四海。

translations.literal: Our lord's heaven-given talent is outstanding, his soaring will pierces the clouds — he is sure to embrace the six directions and unite the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: "Our lord's gifts tower above others and his ambition pierces the clouds — he will surely take the realm and unite the four seas."

sentences.zh: 夫遭風雲之會，不建騰躍之功者，非人豪也。

translations.literal: One who meets the wind and clouds yet builds no soaring achievement is no true hero."
translations.idiomatic: "Who meets such a moment and does not rise with it is no true hero."

sentences.zh: 」遂策名委質，竭誠伏事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pledged his name and devoted himself, serving with full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He then pledged himself and served with whole-hearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時劉顯地廣兵強，跨有朔裔，會其兄弟乖離，共相疑阻。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Xian held broad lands and a strong army, spanning the northern marches; it happened that his brothers were at odds and mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Xian held vast territory and a strong army across the north; his brothers had fallen out and distrusted one another.

sentences.zh: 袞言於太祖曰：「顯志大意高，希冀非望，乃有參天貳地，籠罩宇宙之規。

translations.literal: Gun said to Taizu: "Xian's will is great and his intent high; his hopes are not ordinary — he has designs to match heaven and earth and enfold the universe.
translations.idiomatic: Gun told Taizu, "Xian is proud and ambitious beyond the ordinary — he dreams of rivaling heaven and earth and swallowing the world."

sentences.zh: 吳不并越，將為後患。

translations.literal: If Wu is not united with Yue, it will be a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: "If Wu is not joined with Yue, he will trouble us later."

sentences.zh: 今因其內釁，宜速乘之。

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of their internal strife, we should strike quickly.
translations.idiomatic: "Use their internal strife and strike now."

sentences.zh: 若輕師獨進，或恐越逸。

translations.literal: If a light force advances alone, I fear he may slip away.
translations.idiomatic: "A lone light column may let him escape."

sentences.zh: 可遣使告慕容垂，共相聲援，東西俱舉，勢必擒之。

translations.literal: We could send envoys to tell Murong Chui to join in mutual support; striking east and west together, he is sure to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: "Send word to Murong Chui to join us; attack from east and west together and he is sure to fall."

sentences.zh: 然後總括英雄，撫懷遐邇，此千載一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: Then gather heroes and soothe the distant — this is a moment once in a thousand years and must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: "Then rally the bold and win the far marches — a chance that comes once in a thousand years; do not miss it."

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之，遂破走顯。

translations.literal: Taizu followed this and routed Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took his advice and drove Xian off.

sentences.zh: 又從破賀訥，遂命羣官登勿居山，遊宴終日。

translations.literal: He also followed in defeating He Ne; he then ordered the officials to ascend Wuju Mountain and feast all day.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gun again in defeating He Ne, then ordered the court to climb Wuju Mountain and feast all day.

sentences.zh: 從官及諸部大人請聚石為峰，以記功德，命袞為文。

translations.literal: Attending officials and the great men of the tribes asked to pile stones into a peak to record the achievement; Taizu ordered Gun to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and tribal leaders asked to heap stones into a monument; Taizu had Gun write the inscription.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶之來寇也，袞言於太祖曰：「寶乘滑臺之功，因長子之捷，傾資竭力，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Gun said to Taizu: "Bao rides on the merit of Huatai and the victory at Changzi, pouring out his treasury and strength — he is hard to meet in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Gun told Taizu, "Bao builds on Huatai and Changzi, spending treasury and strength — he is dangerous to meet head-on."

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜羸師卷甲，以侈其心。

translations.literal: In my foolish view we should show a weak army and roll up our armor to swell his pride."
translations.idiomatic: "I would show a weak force and fold our armor away to puff up his pride."

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之，果破之參合。

translations.literal: Taizu followed this and indeed defeated him at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed and crushed him at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangshi he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖南伐，師次中山。

translations.literal: Taizu campaigned south and halted the army at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu marched south and camped at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 袞言於太祖曰：「寶憑三世之資，城池之固，雖皇威震赫，勢必擒殄，然窮兵極武，非王者所宜。

translations.literal: Gun said to Taizu: "Bao relies on three generations' inheritance and his city's strength; though imperial majesty shakes the land and he is sure to be destroyed, exhausting the army to the limit is not what a true king should do.
translations.idiomatic: Gun told Taizu, "Bao rests on three generations and strong walls; though your majesty will surely take him, driving the army to extremity is not a king's way."

sentences.zh: 昔酈生一說，田橫委質；

translations.literal: In old times Li Yiji with one persuasion made Tian Heng submit;
translations.idiomatic: "Long ago Li Yiji with one speech made Tian Heng yield;"

sentences.zh: 魯連飛書，聊將授首。

translations.literal: Lu Zhong's flying letter was enough to make him offer his head.
translations.idiomatic: "Lu Zhong's letter from afar was enough to make a man offer his head."

sentences.zh: 臣誠德非古人，略無奇策，仰憑靈威，庶必有感。

translations.literal: Your subject's virtue is not equal to those ancients and I lack any wondrous stratagem, but relying on your spiritual might, there may yet be a response."
translations.idiomatic: "I am no match for those men and have no clever scheme, yet under your power something may move him."

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: Taizu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 袞遺寶書。

translations.literal: Gun sent Bao a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Gun sent Bao a letter — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 喻以成敗。

translations.literal: He explained success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: He set out the odds of victory and defeat.

sentences.zh: 寶見書大懼，遂奔和龍。

translations.literal: When Bao saw the letter he was greatly afraid and fled to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was terrified by the letter and fled to Helong.

sentences.zh: 既克中山，聽入八議，拜袞奮武將軍、幽州刺史，賜爵臨渭侯。

translations.literal: After Zhongshan was taken, he was admitted to the eight deliberations and made General Who Displays Valor, Inspector of Youzhou, and Marquis of Linwei.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell, Gun entered the eight deliberations and was made General Who Displays Valor, Youzhou inspector, and Marquis of Linwei.

sentences.zh: 袞清儉寡欲，勸課農桑，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Gun was pure and frugal in desire, urging farming and sericulture; the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gun lived plainly and urged farming and silk; the people were settled.

sentences.zh: 天興初，徵還京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後與崔逞答司馬德宗將郗恢書失旨，黜袞為尚書令史。

translations.literal: Later, with Cui Cheng he answered a letter from Jin's Sima Dezong's general Xi Hui in a way that missed the mark; Gun was demoted to clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Cui Cheng drafted a reply to Xi Hui, general under Jin's Sima Dezong, that missed the tone; Gun was demoted to clerk of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 袞遇創業之始，以有才謨見任，率心奉上，不顧嫌疑。

translations.literal: Gun met the founding of the state and, for talent and counsel, was entrusted; he served with an open heart and did not shrink from suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Gun had served from the founding days, trusted for talent and counsel, and gave his heart without fear of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 太祖曾問南州人於袞。

translations.literal: Taizu once asked Gun about men of the southern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once asked Gun about talent from the south.

sentences.zh: 袞與盧溥州里，數談薦之。

translations.literal: Gun and Lu Bo were from the same commandery; he often spoke and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was from the same commandery as Lu Bo and often praised him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又袞未嘗與崔逞相見，聞風稱美。

translations.literal: Gun had also never met Cui Cheng but, hearing his reputation, praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He had never met Cui Cheng either, yet praised him on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 及中山平，盧溥聚黨為逆，崔逞答書不允，並乖本言，故忿之。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Bo gathered a faction in rebellion and Cui Cheng's reply letter was not compliant — both contrary to his earlier words, so he resented them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Bo raised a faction in revolt and Cui Cheng's reply was defiant; both belied what Gun had said, and he bore them a grudge.

sentences.zh: 袞年過七十，闔門守靜，手執經書，刊定乖失，愛好人物，善誘無倦，士類以此高之。

translations.literal: When Gun passed seventy, the whole household kept to quiet; in hand he held the classics, collating deviations and errors, loving men of worth, skilled at drawing them on without weariness—the scholarly class for this held him high.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, Gun kept his whole household in quiet; he held the classics in hand, collated what had gone astray, delighted in men of talent, and guided them without tiring—the learned held him in high esteem for it.

sentences.zh: 永興二年疾篤，上疏曰：「臣既庸人，志無殊操，值太祖誕膺期運，天地始開，參戎氛霧之初，馳驅革命之會，託翼鄧林，寄鱗溟海，遂荷恩寵，榮兼出內。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxing his illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant is a mediocre man, his will without special constancy; it fell to me to live when the Founding Ancestor received Heaven's mandate and the world first opened—I shared in the mist of war at the beginning and galloped through the season of revolution, trusting my wings to the Deng grove and my scales to the deep sea; thus I bore favor and grace, glory reaching within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing his illness turned grave; he submitted a memorial: "I am a mediocre man without special resolve, yet I lived when the Founding Ancestor received Heaven's mandate and the world first opened. I shared the war-mist at the start and rode through the season of revolution, trusting my wings to the sacred grove and my scales to the deep sea, and so bore favor whose glory reached within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飛九五，仍參顧問，曾無微誠，塵山露海。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty ascended the dragon throne, I still took part in counsel, yet never offered the slightest sincerity—dust piled like mountains, dew spread like seas.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne I still sat in counsel, yet never offered the slightest sincerity—my debt piled like mountains, my thanks spread like seas.

sentences.zh: 今舊疾彌留，氣力虛頓，天罰有罪，將填溝壑。

translations.literal: Now my old illness lingers on, my strength empty and spent; Heaven punishes the guilty—I am about to fill the gully and ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Now my old illness lingers and my strength is spent; Heaven punishes guilt, and I am about to fill a ditch.

sentences.zh: 然犬馬戀主，敢不盡言。

translations.literal: Yet the dog and horse love their master—I dare not withhold my words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dog and horse love their master, and I dare not withhold my words.

sentences.zh: 方今中夏雖平，九域未一，西有不賓之羌，南有逆命之虜，岷蜀殊風，遼海異教。

translations.literal: At present the central lands are at peace, yet the nine regions are not one; in the west are unsubmissive Qiang, in the south rebels who defy command; Min and Shu have other customs, Liao and the sea other teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The central lands are at peace, yet the nine regions are not one: unsubmissive Qiang in the west, rebels in the south, other customs in Min and Shu, other faiths along Liao and the sea.

sentences.zh: 雖天挺明聖，撥亂乘時，而因幾撫會，實須經略。

translations.literal: Though Heaven has raised a bright sage who sets disorder aright and rides the times, to seize the moment and soothe the conjunction truly requires strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven has raised a bright sage to set disorder aright and ride the times, seizing the moment and steering events still demands strategy.

sentences.zh: 介焉易失，功在人謀。

translations.literal: The hinge is easily lost; achievement lies in human counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The hinge slips easily; achievement rests on human counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏願恢崇叡道，克廣德心，使揖讓與干戈並陳，文德與武功俱運，則太平之化，康哉之美，復隆於今，不獨前世。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that sagely Way be restored and lofty, that virtue's heart be broadened, so yielding and arms are set forth together, civil virtue and martial achievement both put in motion—then the transformation of great peace and the beauty of "How grand!" would rise again in our day, not only in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the sagely Way be lifted high and the heart of virtue broadened, so courtesy and arms stand together and civil and martial power move as one—then the age of great peace and the cry of "How grand!" would rise again today, not only in ages past.

sentences.zh: 昔子囊將終，寄言城郢；

translations.literal: Of old, when Zi Nang was near death, he left word to defend Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Of old, when Zi Nang was near death, he left word to defend Ying; (record).

sentences.zh: 荀偃辭唅，遺恨在齊。

translations.literal: when Xun Yan took leave of breath, his regret remained in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: when Xun Yan drew his last breath, his regret still lay in Qi.

sentences.zh: 臣雖闇劣，敢忘前志，魂而有靈，結草泉壤。

translations.literal: Your servant, though dim and weak, dares not forget the former resolve; if my soul has spirit, I shall tie grass in the springs below.
translations.idiomatic: I am dim and weak, yet dare not forget that resolve; if my soul has spirit, I shall tie grass in the land below."

sentences.zh: 」後數日卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: " Several days later he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 後世祖追錄舊勳，遣大鴻臚即墓策贈太保，諡曰文康公。

translations.literal: Later the Shizu emperor, recording old merit, sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with a patent enfeoffing him posthumously as Grand Mentor and titling him Duke Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Shizu, recording old merit, sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with a patent making him Grand Mentor posthumously and titling him Duke Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 子溫，外都大官、廣寧太守。

translations.literal: His son Wen was Outer Metropolitan Food Officer and Administrator of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen served as Outer Metropolitan Food Officer and Administrator of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子貳興，昌黎太守。

translations.literal: His son Erxing was Administrator of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Erxing was Administrator of Changli — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 溫弟楷，州主簿。

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Kai was a provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's younger brother Kai was a provincial chief clerk — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 子誕，有學尚，性尤雅直。

translations.literal: His son Dan was learned and principled, his nature especially refined and upright.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan was learned and principled, his nature especially refined and upright — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 初與高允同時被徵，後除中書侍郎、通直散騎常侍、建威將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned together with Gao Yun; later he was made Secretariat Gentleman, Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, and General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was summoned together with Gao Yun; later he was made Secretariat Gentleman, Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, and General Who Establishes Might — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 賜爵容城子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 袞次子度，少有志尚，襲爵臨渭侯。

translations.literal: Gun's second son Du, in youth ambitious and high-minded, inherited the fief as Marquis of Linwei.
translations.idiomatic: Gun's second son Du, ambitious from youth, inherited the fief as Marquis of Linwei.

sentences.zh: 上谷太守，入為武昌王師。

translations.literal: Administrator of Shanggu; he entered court as tutor to the Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Shanggu, then entered court as tutor to the Prince of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，除使持節，都督幽州廣陽、安樂二郡諸軍事，平東將軍，崎城鎮都大將，又轉和龍鎮都大將，所在著稱。

translations.literal: He was further made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, commissioned with the staff of authority as Commander over military affairs of Youzhou's Guangyang and Anle commanderies, General Who Pacifies the East, Metropolitan Commander of Qicheng, then transferred as Metropolitan Commander of Helong—wherever he served he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, then commissioned with the staff of authority as commander over military affairs of Youzhou's Guangyang and Anle, General Who Pacifies the East, Metropolitan Commander of Qicheng, then transferred to Metropolitan Commander of Helong—wherever he served he won renown.

sentences.zh: 還朝為中都大官。

translations.literal: Returning to court he became Metropolitan Food Officer of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he became Metropolitan Food Officer of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征東大將軍、冀州刺史，諡康侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Ji, titled Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Ji, titled Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子陵，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ling inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling inherited the fief — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 後為赤城典作都將。

translations.literal: Later he was Metropolitan Director of Works at Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Metropolitan Director of Works at Chicheng — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子狀，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhuang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuang inherited — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 為中散。

translations.literal: He was a Palace Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Palace Scribe — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子法，襲。

translations.literal: His son Fa inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fa inherited — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太和中，例降為伯。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，除懷荒鎮金城戍將。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was made garrison commander of Huaihuang at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Shizong's time he was made garrison commander of Huaihuang at Jincheng — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 陵弟延，散騎常侍、左將軍、庫部尚書。

translations.literal: Ling's younger brother Yan was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Left General, and Minister of the Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's younger brother Yan was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Left General, and Minister of the Storehouses — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 賜爵永寧侯。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Yongning — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 延弟白澤，[2]年十一，遭母憂，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Bai Ze,[2] at eleven years, met his mother's death; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Bai Ze[2], at eleven, lost his mother; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu heard of it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu heard of it and commended him — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 長而好學博通，敏於當世。

translations.literal: Grown, he loved learning and was broadly versed, keen in affairs of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning, was broadly versed, and keen in affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，除中散，遷殿中曹給事中，甚見寵任，參預機密。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was made Palace Scribe, then moved to Attendant of the Palace Bureau, and was greatly favored and trusted, taking part in secret counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was made Palace Scribe, then Attendant of the Palace Bureau, greatly favored and trusted and drawn into secret counsel.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，顯祖引見羣臣議之。

translations.literal: Later the Rouran raided the border; Emperor Xianzu summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Rouran raided the border; Emperor Xianzu summoned the ministers to discuss it — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射元目辰進曰：「若車駕親行，恐京師危懼，不如持重，固守自安。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Muchén advanced and said: "If the imperial carriage goes in person, I fear the capital will be shaken with alarm; better to hold steady and secure oneself by defense.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Muchén advanced and said: "If Your Majesty goes in person, the capital may panic; better to hold steady and keep to defense.

sentences.zh: 虜懸軍深入，糧無繼運，以臣量之，自退不久，遣將追擊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: The foe has driven deep with an army on the march; their grain cannot follow—by my reckoning they will withdraw before long; send generals in pursuit and crushing them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has marched deep with no grain to follow; by my reckoning they will soon withdraw—send generals in pursuit and victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 」白澤曰：「陛下欽明則天，比蹤前聖，而蠢爾荒愚，輕犯王略。

translations.literal: Bai Ze said: "Your Majesty, reverent and bright as Heaven, treads the tracks of former sages, yet these fools of the wilds in their ignorance lightly violate the royal plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ze said: "Your Majesty, reverent and bright as Heaven, treads the tracks of former sages, yet these wild fools in their ignorance lightly violate the royal plan.

sentences.zh: 寇乃顛沛於遠圖，我將宴安於近毒，仰惟神略，則不然矣。

translations.literal: The raiders toil in distant schemes while our generals feast in nearby peril—measured by divine strategy, that cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders toil in distant schemes while our generals feast amid nearby danger—measured by divine strategy, that cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 今若鑾輿親動，賊必望麾崩散，寧容仰挫神兵，坐而縱敵。

translations.literal: If now the imperial carriage moves in person, the bandits will surely scatter at the sight of the banners—how could we bear to let divine arms be checked and sit idle while the foe goes free?
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage moves now, the bandits will scatter at the banners—how could we let divine arms be checked and sit idle while the foe escapes?

sentences.zh: 萬乘之尊，嬰城自守，進失可乘之機，退非無前之義，惟陛下留神。

translations.literal: The honor of ten thousand chariots, besieged in its own walls—advancing, you lose a chance that can be seized; retreating, you fall short of the way of pressing forward without rival. I beg Your Majesty to ponder this."
translations.idiomatic: The honor of ten thousand chariots, walled up at home—advance and you lose a chance that can be seized; retreat and you fall short of pressing forward without rival. I beg Your Majesty to ponder this."

sentences.zh: 」顯祖從之，遂大破虜眾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu followed this counsel and thereupon utterly broke the barbarian host.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu followed this counsel and utterly broke the barbarian host.

sentences.zh: 白澤本字鍾葵，顯祖賜名白澤，納其女為嬪。

translations.literal: Bai Ze's original name was Zhongkui; Emperor Xianzu bestowed the name Bai Ze and took his daughter into the inner palace as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ze's original name was Zhongkui; Emperor Xianzu bestowed the name Bai Ze and took his daughter into the inner palace as a consort — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 出行雍州刺史，清心少欲，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Sent out as Inspector of Yong Province, he kept his heart clear and his desires few; officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Inspector of Yong Province, he kept his heart clear and his desires few; officials and people were at peace under him — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 顯祖詔諸監臨之官，所監治受羊一口、酒一斛者，罪至大辟，與者以從坐論。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu decreed that any supervising official who in his jurisdiction received one sheep or one jar of wine would be guilty of a capital offense, and the giver would be judged as an accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu decreed that any supervising official who in his jurisdiction received one sheep or one jar of wine would face capital punishment, and the giver would be judged as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 糾告得尚書已下罪狀者，各隨所糾官輕重而授之。

translations.literal: Whoever reported and proved guilt among those from the Masters of Writing downward would be given office according to the weight of the official denounced.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever reported and proved guilt among officials from the Masters of Writing downward would receive office according to the rank of the official denounced.

sentences.zh: 白澤上表諫曰：「伏見詔書，禁尚書以下受禮者刑身，糾之者代職。

translations.literal: Bai Ze submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "I bow and have seen the edict forbidding gifts to those from the Masters of Writing downward on pain of bodily punishment, with the accuser to take the denounced man's post.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ze submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have seen the edict that punishes Masters of Writing and below who accept gifts with death, and gives the accuser the denounced man's post.

sentences.zh: 伏惟三載考績，黜陟幽明，斯乃不易之令軌，百王之通式。

translations.literal: I reflect that the triennial review of achievement, demoting and promoting the hidden and the clear, is an unchanging statute and the common pattern of a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the triennial review of achievement, demoting the obscure and promoting the clear, is an unchanging statute and the common pattern of a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 今之都曹，古之公卿也，皆翊扶萬幾，讚徽百揆，風化藉此而平，治道由茲而穆。

translations.literal: Today's Metropolitan Bureau is the public ministers of old; all assist in the myriad affairs, praise and harmonize the hundred duties—through them custom is leveled and the way of rule made tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Metropolitan Bureau is the public ministers of old; all assist in the myriad affairs and harmonize the hundred duties—through them custom is leveled and the way of rule made tranquil.

sentences.zh: 且周之下士，尚有代耕，況皇朝貴仕，而服勤無報，豈所謂祖襲堯舜，憲章文武者乎？

translations.literal: Even Zhou's lowest officers still had substitute fields for their labor—how much more the honored offices of our dynasty, serving diligently yet receiving no reward; can this be called inheriting Yao and Shun and taking Wen and Wu as one's model?"
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou's lowest officers still had substitute fields for their labor—how much more our honored offices, serving diligently yet unrewarded; can this be called inheriting Yao and Shun and taking Wen and Wu as one's model?"

sentences.zh: 羊酒之罰，若行不已，臣恐姦人闚望，忠臣懈節。

translations.literal: If the penalty of sheep and wine is carried out without end, I fear schemers will watch for their chance and loyal ministers slacken in constancy.
translations.idiomatic: If the penalty of sheep and wine goes on without end, I fear schemers will watch for their chance and loyal ministers will slacken.

sentences.zh: 而欲使事靜民安，治清務簡，至於委任責成，下民難辯。

translations.literal: Yet you wish affairs quiet and the people at peace, government clear and tasks simple—yet entrusting responsibility and demanding results, the lower people are hard put to argue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you wish affairs quiet and the people at peace, government clear and tasks simple—yet in entrusting responsibility and demanding results, the lower people are hard put to argue.

sentences.zh: [3]如臣愚量，請依律令舊法，稽同前典，班祿酬廉，首去亂羣，常刑無赦。

translations.literal: [3] By my foolish reckoning, I ask that the old laws and statutes be followed, checked against former canons, salaries paid to reward integrity, the disorderly crowd removed first, and ordinary punishments never pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: [3] By my foolish reckoning, I ask that the old laws be followed, checked against former canons, salaries paid to reward integrity, the disorderly crowd removed first, and ordinary punishments never pardoned.

sentences.zh: 苟能如此，則升平之軌，期月可望，刑措之風，三年必致矣。

translations.literal: If this can be done, the track of ascending peace may be looked for within a month, and the wind of laying aside punishments will surely arrive in three years."
translations.idiomatic: If this can be done, the track of ascending peace may be looked for within a month, and the wind of laying aside punishments will arrive in three years."

sentences.zh: 」顯祖納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu accepted it — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太和初，懷州民伊祁苟初三十餘人謀反，將殺刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, more than thirty men of Huai Province led by Yi Qigou plotted rebellion and meant to kill the inspector.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe, more than thirty men of Huai Province led by Yi Qigou plotted rebellion and meant to kill the inspector — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 文明太后欲盡誅一城之民。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming wished to execute the whole city's people.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming wished to execute the whole city's people — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 白澤諫曰：「臣聞上天愛物之生，明王重民之命，故殺一人而取天下，仁者不為。

translations.literal: Bai Ze remonstrated, saying: "I have heard that Heaven loves the life of things and the bright king values the people's lives; therefore to kill one man and take the realm is not what the benevolent do.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ze remonstrated: "I have heard that Heaven loves the life of things and the bright king values the people's lives; to kill one man and take the realm is not what the benevolent do.

sentences.zh: 且周書父子兄弟，罪不相及，今羣凶肆虐，轘裂誅盡，合城無辜，奈何極辟。

translations.literal: Moreover the Zhou Documents say that father, son, and brothers do not share guilt for one another's crimes; now the ringleaders run wild and are torn apart and put to the sword, yet the whole city is innocent—how can extreme punishment reach so far?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Zhou Documents say father, son, and brothers do not share one another's guilt; now the ringleaders are torn apart and put to the sword, yet the whole city is innocent—how can extreme punishment reach so far?

sentences.zh: 不誣十室，而況一州，或有忠焉，或有仁者，若淫刑濫及，殺忠與仁，斯乃西伯所以歎息於九侯，孔子所以回輪於河上。

translations.literal: Do not wrong ten households—how much more a whole province; there may be loyal men or benevolent men among them; if excessive punishment sweeps them in, killing the loyal and the benevolent, this is why the Western Earl sighed over the Nine Marquises and Confucius turned his carriage at the river.
translations.idiomatic: Do not wrong ten households—how much more a whole province; there may be loyal or benevolent men among them; if excessive punishment sweeps them in and kills the loyal and benevolent, this is why the Western Earl sighed over the Nine Marquises and Confucius turned his carriage at the river.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖德昭明殷鑒，水鏡前禮，[4]止迅烈之怒，抑雷霆之威，則溥天知幸矣。

translations.literal: I bow and reflect that sagely virtue is bright as a mirror and water-polished by former ritual,[4] restraining sudden wrath and checking thunder's might—then all under Heaven would know fortune."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to consider that sagely virtue is bright as a mirror and water-polished by former ritual,[4] restraining sudden wrath and checking thunder's might—then all under Heaven would know fortune."

sentences.zh: 昔厲防民口，卒滅宗姬；

translations.literal: Of old King Li stopped the people's mouths and at last extinguished the house of Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Of old King Li stopped the people's mouths and at last extinguished the house of Ji; (record).

sentences.zh: 文聽輿頌，終摧強楚。

translations.literal: King Wen listened to cart-songs and in the end crushed mighty Chu.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen listened to cart-songs and in the end crushed mighty Chu — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 願不以人廢言，留神省察。

translations.literal: I wish that you not reject words because of the speaker—leave your mind to examine them."
translations.idiomatic: I wish you not reject words because of the speaker—leave your mind to examine them."

sentences.zh: 」太后從之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager followed this — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，遷殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太和五年卒，詔賜帛一千匹、粟三千石，遣侍御史營護喪事，冊贈鎮南將軍、相州刺史、廣平公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he died; an edict granted a thousand bolts of silk and three thousand shi of grain, sent a attendant censor to oversee the funeral, and by patent enfeoffed him posthumously as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Xiang, and Duke of Guangping, titled Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he died; an edict granted a thousand bolts of silk and three thousand shi of grain, sent an attendant censor to oversee the funeral, and by patent enfeoffed him posthumously as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Xiang, and Duke of Guangping, titled Jian.

sentences.zh: 長子倫，字天念。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，入侍左右。

translations.literal: Past ten years of age, he attended at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Past ten, he attended at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 稍遷護軍長史、員外常侍，轉大司農少卿、燕州大中正。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Guard Army, Outer Attendant, then Vice Director of the Grand Granary and Grand Rectifier of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Guard Army, Outer Attendant, then Vice Director of the Grand Granary and Grand Rectifier of Yan Province — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，蠕蠕主醜奴遣使來朝，抗敵國之書，不修臣敬。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era the Rouran ruler Chounu sent envoys to court with a letter treating the state as an equal power and without the courtesy due a subject.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era the Rouran ruler Chounu sent envoys to court with a letter treating the state as an equal and without subject courtesy.

sentences.zh: 朝議將依漢答匈奴故事，遣使報之。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to follow the Han precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion wished to follow the Han precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 倫表曰：

translations.literal: Lun submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lun submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之聖王，疆理物土，辨章要甸，荒遐之俗，政所不及。

translations.literal: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity divided the land and regulated things, distinguished the chief districts, and lands of distant wilds were outside what government could reach.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity divided the land and regulated things, distinguished the chief districts, and distant wilds lay outside what government could reach.

sentences.zh: 故禮有壹見之文，書著羈縻之事。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual has the text of a single audience, and the Documents record the matter of loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ritual has the text of a single audience, and the Documents record the matter of loose reins — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太祖以神武之姿，聖明之略，經略帝圖，日有不暇，遂令竪子遊魂一方，亦由中國多虞，急諸華而緩夷狄也。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, with divine martial bearing and sagely bright design, laid out the imperial plan day by day without rest; thus a stripling's wandering soul was left on one side—also because the central lands had many troubles and urgency lay with the Hua while the Yi and Di could wait.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor, with divine martial bearing and sagely design, laid out the imperial plan day by day without rest; thus a stripling's wandering soul was left on one side—also because the central lands had many troubles and urgency lay with the Hua while the Yi and Di could wait.

sentences.zh: 高祖光宅土中，業隆卜世，赫雷霆之威，振熊羆之旅，方役南轅，未遑北伐。

translations.literal: Gaozu shed light on the central land and his enterprise towered for generations; he shook thunder's might and roused the bear-and-tiger hosts, yet was campaigning south and had no leisure to march north.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu shed light on the central land and his enterprise towered for generations; he shook thunder's might and roused the bear-and-tiger hosts, yet was campaigning south and had no leisure to march north — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 昔舊京烽起，虜使在郊，主上按劍，璽書不出。

translations.literal: Of old, when the old capital flared with alarm, barbarian envoys were at the suburbs; the sovereign gripped his sword and the imperial letter did not go forth.
