translations.idiomatic: Of old, when the old capital flared with alarm, barbarian envoys were at the suburbs; the sovereign gripped his sword and the imperial letter did not go forth — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 世宗運籌帷幄，開境揚旌，衣裳所及，舟車萬里。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong plotted within the tent and opened the borders, raising banners; wherever robe and cap reached, boat and cart ran ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong plotted within the tent and opened the borders, raising banners; wherever robe and cap reached, boat and cart ran ten thousand li — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 于時醜類款關，上亦述尊遺志。

translations.literal: At that time the ugly sort knocked at the gate, and the sovereign too followed the honored departed will.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarians knocked at the gate, and the sovereign too followed the honored departed will.

sentences.zh: 今大明臨朝，澤及行葦，國富兵強，能言率職。

translations.literal: Now great brightness faces the court, grace reaches the traveling reed; the state is rich, the army strong, and those who can speak come to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Now great brightness faces the court, grace reaches the traveling reed; the state is rich, the army strong, and those who can speak come to duty — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 何憚而為之，何求而行此？

translations.literal: What is there to fear in doing this, what is sought in acting thus?
translations.idiomatic: What is there to fear in doing this, what is sought in acting thus? (record).

sentences.zh: 往日蕭衍通敬求和，以誠肅未純，抑而不許。

translations.literal: In former days Xiao Yan sent envoys seeking peace with sincere respect; because his sincerity was not pure, it was suppressed and not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In former days Xiao Yan sent envoys seeking peace with sincere respect; because his sincerity was not pure, it was suppressed and not granted — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 先帝棄戎於前，陛下交夷於後，無乃上乖高祖之心，下違世宗之意？

translations.literal: The former emperor cast off arms before, and Your Majesty treats the Yi after—will this not be above against Gaozu's heart and below against Shizong's intent?
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor cast off arms before, and Your Majesty treats the Yi after—will this not be above against Gaozu's heart and below against Shizong's intent? (record).

sentences.zh: 且虜雖慕德，亦來觀我，懼之以強，儻即歸附，示之以弱，窺覦或起，春秋所謂「以我卜也」。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us; awe them with strength and they may at once submit; show them weakness and covetous watching may arise—the Spring and Autumn Annals calls this "taking us as the augury."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us; awe them with strength and they may at once submit; show them weakness and covetous watching may arise—the Spring and Autumn Annals calls this "taking us as the augury." (record).

sentences.zh: 又小人難近，夷狄無親，疏之則怨，狎之則侮，其所由來久矣。

translations.literal: Again, petty men are hard to approach and the Yi and Di have no kinship; keep them distant and they resent, draw them close and they insult—this has long been their way.
translations.idiomatic: Again, petty men are hard to approach and the Yi and Di have no kinship; keep them distant and they resent, draw them close and they insult—this has long been their way — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 是以高祖、世宗知其若此，來既莫逆，去又不追。

translations.literal: Therefore Gaozu and Shizong knew it was so: when they came, they did not press intimacy; when they went, they did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Gaozu and Shizong knew it was so: when they came, they did not press intimacy; when they went, they did not pursue — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 不一之義，於是乎在。

translations.literal: The meaning of not making one rule lies here.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of not making one rule lies here — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 必其委贄玉帛之辰，屈膝蕃方之禮，則可豐其勞賄，籍以珍物。

translations.literal: Only when they come with tribute of jade and silks and bend the knee in the rites of the frontier may their labor be richly rewarded and their goods entered in the register.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they come with tribute of jade and silks and bend the knee in the rites of the frontier may their labor be richly rewarded and their goods entered in the register — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 至於王人遠役，銜命虜庭，優以匹敵之尊，加之相望之寵，恐徒生虜慢，無益聖朝。

translations.literal: As for the king's man sent on distant service, bearing command in the barbarian court, honored with the standing of an equal and further given the favor of mutual regard—I fear it will only breed barbarian insolence and do the holy court no good.
translations.idiomatic: As for the king's man sent on distant service, bearing command in the barbarian court, honored as an equal and further given the favor of mutual regard—I fear it will only breed barbarian insolence and do the holy court no good.

sentences.zh: 假令選眾而舉，使乎稱職，資酈生之辯，騁終軍之辭，憑軾下齊，長纓繫越。

translations.literal: Suppose one chose the multitude and raised a worthy envoy, lent the eloquence of Li Yiji, let loose the words of Zhong Jun, leaned on the carriage rail to bring Qi down, and with a long tassel bound Yue—if it differed from former times, one would still be unwilling; how much less exalt them to the utmost honor and extend them feast and friendship?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose one chose the multitude and raised a worthy envoy, lent the eloquence of Li Yiji, let loose the words of Zhong Jun, leaned on the carriage rail to bring Qi down, and with a long tassel bound Yue—if it differed from former times, one would still be unwilling; how much less exalt them to utmost honor and extend them feast and friendship?

sentences.zh: 苟異曩時，猶為不願，而況極之以隆崇，申之以宴好，臣雖下愚，輒敢固執。

translations.literal: Your servant, though low and foolish, still dares to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: I am low and foolish, yet still dare to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 若事不獲已，應頒制詔，示其上下之儀，宰臣致書，諷以歸順之道。

translations.literal: If the matter cannot be avoided, there should be issued an imperial edict showing the upper and lower etiquette, and the chief minister should send a letter admonishing them in the way of returning to obedience.
translations.idiomatic: If the matter cannot be avoided, an imperial edict should show the etiquette of superior and inferior, and the chief minister should send a letter admonishing them in the way of returning to obedience.

sentences.zh: 若聽受忠誨，明我話言，則萬乘之盛不失位於域中，天子之聲必籠罩於無外。

translations.literal: If you heed loyal counsel and clarify my words, then the grandeur of the myriad-chariot throne shall not lose its place within the realm, and the Son of Heaven's renown shall surely enfold all beyond.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will hear loyal counsel and weigh my words, the throne's majesty will keep its seat at the center of the world, and imperial renown will cover every border.

sentences.zh: 脫或未從，焉能損益。

translations.literal: If perchance you do not follow, how could there be gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not, nothing is gained or lost by it.

sentences.zh: 徐舞干戚以招之，敷文德而懷遠。

translations.literal: Slowly brandish shield and axe to summon them; spread civil virtue to win the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Let shield and axe be danced slowly to draw them in; let civil virtue spread until the far peoples come of themselves.

sentences.zh: 如迷心不已，或肆犬羊，則當命辛李之將，勒衞霍之師，蕩定雲沙，掃清逋孽，飲馬瀚海之濱，鏤石燕然之上，開都護，置戊己，斯亦陛下之高功，不世之盛事。

translations.literal: If the deluded heart does not cease, or they unleash dog-and-goat fury, then command generals like Xin and Li, marshal armies like Wei and Huo, pacify the drifting sands, sweep clear fleeing rebels, water horses on Hanhai's shore, carve stone on Mount Yanran, open Protector-General offices, set Wu and Ji garrisons — this too would be Your Majesty's lofty achievement, an unparalleled triumph.
translations.idiomatic: If their hearts stay blind and they run wild as dogs and goats, then send generals in the mold of Xin and Li, hosts like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing — still the drifting sands, purge the fugitive rebels, water horses beside Hanhai, cut stone on Mount Yanran, open protectorates and set Wu-Ji garrisons. That too would be Your Majesty's high merit, a triumph without peer.

sentences.zh: 如思按甲養民，務農安邊之術，經國之防，豈可以戎夷兼并，而遽虧典制。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thinks to sheathe armor and nurture the people, pursue farming and secure the borders — the defenses that govern the state — how can barbarian merger be allowed to suddenly damage canonical institutions.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to rest the armies, cherish the people, farm the fields, and seal the marches — the long walls of statecraft — how can you let barbarian absorption wreck the rites overnight?

sentences.zh: 將取笑於當時，貽醜於來葉。

translations.literal: You will become a jest in your own age and leave a stain for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: You will be laughed at in your own day and shamed in the histories to come.

sentences.zh: 昔文公請隧，襄后有言；

translations.literal: In olden days Duke Wen of Jin requested the tunnel rite, and Duchess Wen spoke against it;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Duke Wen of Jin asked for the royal burial tunnel, and Duchess Wen of Jin refused him;

sentences.zh: 荊莊問鼎，王孫是抑。

translations.literal: King Zhuang of Chu asked about the Nine Cauldrons, and Wangsun Man rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhuang of Chu inquired after the Nine Cauldrons, and Wangsun Man turned him back.

sentences.zh: 以古方今，竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Measuring the present by antiquity, I venture to think Your Majesty should not take this course.
translations.idiomatic: Set the present beside those tales, and I dare say Your Majesty should not take this path.

sentences.zh: 又陛下方欲禮神岷瀆，致禮衡山，登稽嶺，窺蒼梧，而反與夷虜之君，酋渠之長，結昆弟之忻，抗分庭之義，將何以瞰文命之遐景，迹重華之高風者哉？

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is about to worship the spirits of Min and the River Fu, perform rites at Mount Heng, ascend Mount Ji, gaze toward Cangwu — yet you would instead bind yourself in brotherly joy with chiefs of barbarian captives and heads of alien clans, set yourself against the etiquette of sharing the court as equals — how then can you survey the far vistas of perfected civilizing influence, or follow the lofty conduct of Emperor Shun?
translations.idiomatic: You are about to sacrifice to Min and the Fu River, pay rites at Mount Heng, climb Mount Ji, look toward Cangwu — yet you would clasp barbarian kings and alien chieftains as sworn brothers and meet them as equals under one roof. How then will you trace the wide horizon of Yu's civilizing work, or walk in the high footsteps of Emperor Shun?

sentences.zh: 臣以為報使甚失如彼，不報甚得如此。

translations.literal: I hold that to receive their envoys would be greatly wrong like that; not to receive them would be greatly right like this.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that to answer their embassy as proposed would be a grave error; to refuse it would be the wiser course.

sentences.zh: 願留須臾之聽，察愚臣之言。

translations.literal: I beg you to grant a moment's hearing and examine this foolish minister's words.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a moment of your ear to weigh this humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 出為後將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: He left office as Rear General and Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as rear general and inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除燕州大中正。

translations.literal: On return to court he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made chief rectifier of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遷太常少卿，不拜，轉大司農卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was moved to Vice Minister of Ceremonials but declined the post, and was transferred to Minister of Grand Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang came to the throne he was offered vice minister of ceremonials but declined, and was shifted to minister of grand granaries.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post.

sentences.zh: 倫弟恩，奉朝請，員外郎。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother En was an attendant at court audience and an outer-office gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother En served as court attendant and outer-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 白澤弟庫，瀛州刺史、宜陽侯。

translations.literal: Baize's younger brother Ku was Inspector of Yingzhou and Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Baize's younger brother Ku was inspector of Yingzhou and Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 庫長子蘭，累遷龍驤將軍，行光州事。

translations.literal: Ku's eldest son Lan rose through posts to Dragon-Charging General, acting governor of Guangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ku's eldest son Lan rose step by step to dragon-charging general and acting governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘭弟修虎，都牧、駕部二曹給事中，上谷公，司農少卿。

translations.literal: Lan's younger brother Xiuhu was a supervisor in the Directorate of Herds and Transport Departments, given-office gentleman, Duke of Shanggu, and Vice Minister of Grand Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's younger brother Xiuhu was supervisor in the directorates of herds and transport, a given-office gentleman, Duke of Shanggu, and vice minister of grand granaries.

sentences.zh: 奉使柔玄，察民疾苦。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Rouxuan to examine the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Rouxuan to inquire into the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 遷平北將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies the north and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 度弟太，平西將軍、荊州刺史、俎陽侯。

translations.literal: Du's younger brother Tai was General Who Stabilizes the West, Inspector of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Zuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du's younger brother Tai was general who stabilizes the west, inspector of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Zuyang.

sentences.zh: 太弟那，寧遠將軍、雍城鎮將。

translations.literal: Tai's younger brother Na was General of Pacifying the Distance and garrison commandant of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's younger brother Na was general of pacifying the distance and garrison commandant of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 崔玄伯，清河東武城人也，名犯高祖廟諱，魏司空林六世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanbo was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe. His personal name violated the Founding Emperor's temple taboo. He was the sixth-generation descendant of Wei Minister of Works Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanbo came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe. His birth name broke the Founding Emperor's temple taboo; he was sixth in descent from Wei's minister of works, Cui Lin.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，仕石虎，官至司徒左長史、關內侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue served Shi Hu, reaching the posts of Chief Clerk of the Left in the Secretariat and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue served Shi Hu to chief clerk of the left in the secretariat and marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 父潛，仕慕容暐，為黃門侍郎，並有才學之稱。

translations.literal: His father Qian served Murong Hui as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and both were famed for learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian served Murong Hui as gentleman at the yellow gate; father and son were both famed for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 玄伯少有儁才，號曰冀州神童。

translations.literal: Xuanbo in youth had brilliant talent and was called the prodigy of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xuanbo showed rare brilliance and was called the prodigy of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 苻融牧冀州，虛心禮敬，拜陽平公侍郎，領冀州從事，管征東記室。

translations.literal: When Fu Rong governed Ji Province he treated Xuanbo with courtesy, made him Gentleman of the Yangping Duke's household, a staff member of Ji Province, and head of the eastern campaign secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Rong held Ji Province he honored Xuanbo, made him gentleman of the Yangping duke's household, a Ji staff officer, and head of the eastern campaign secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出總庶事，入為賓友，眾務修理，處斷無滯。

translations.literal: Whether overseeing outside affairs or serving within as a companion, he put every task in order and judged without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Whether he ran affairs in the field or sat as a companion at court, every task fell into order and no decision lagged.

sentences.zh: 苻堅聞而奇之，徵為太子舍人，辭以母疾不就，左遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian heard and marveled, he summoned him as Attendant to the Heir Apparent; citing his mother's illness he did not go, and was demoted to Assistant in the Office for Compiling the Dynastic Record.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, hearing of him, summoned him as attendant to the heir apparent; Xuanbo pleaded his mother's illness and would not go, and was demoted to assistant in the office for compiling the dynastic record.

sentences.zh: 苻丕牧冀州，為征東功曹。

translations.literal: When Fu Pi governed Ji Province, Xuanbo served as merit-recording staff officer on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Pi governed Ji Province, Xuanbo served as merit-recording staff officer on the eastern campaign — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太原郝軒，世名知人，稱玄伯有王佐之才，近代所未有也。

translations.literal: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, famed through generations for knowing men, said Xuanbo had the talent to assist a king — unmatched in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, whose house was famed for judging men, said Xuanbo had king-making talent such as the age had not seen.

sentences.zh: 堅亡，避難於齊魯之間，為丁零翟釗及司馬昌明叛將張願所留縶。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian fell, he took refuge between Qi and Lu, and was detained by the Dingling chieftain Zhai Zhao and the rebel general of Sima Changming, Zhang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian's rule collapsed he fled between Qi and Lu and was held by the Dingling chieftain Zhai Zhao and by Zhang Yuan, rebel general of Sima Changming.

sentences.zh: 郝軒歎曰：「斯人而遇斯時，不因扶搖之勢，而與鷃雀飛沉，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Hao Xuan sighed: "Such a man meeting such a time — without the soaring wind's force he sinks and flies with sparrows. How regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xuan sighed: "A man like this in a time like this — without the wind that lifts him he must sink and rise with sparrows. What a waste!

sentences.zh: 」慕容垂以為吏部郎、尚書左丞、高陽內史。

translations.literal: " Murong Chui appointed him Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel, Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat, and Inner Magistrate of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Chui then made him gentleman in the ministry of personnel, left deputy director of the secretariat, and inner magistrate of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 所歷著稱，立身雅正，與世不羣，雖在兵亂，猶勵志篤學，不以資產為意，妻子不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was praised; upright in bearing and set apart from the world; even amid military chaos he drove himself to study and did not care for property — wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he won praise; upright and apart from the crowd, he kept to his books even in war and cared nothing for wealth — wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 太祖征慕容寶，次於常山，玄伯棄郡，東走海濱。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Murong Bao and halted at Mount Chang, Xuanbo abandoned his commandery and fled east toward the seacoast.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched on Murong Bao and halted at Mount Chang, Xuanbo left his commandery and fled east toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞其名，遣騎追求，執送於軍門，引見與語，悅之，以為黃門侍郎，與張袞對總機要，草創制度。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had long heard his name, sent horsemen in pursuit, had him brought to the army gate and received him; spoke with him and was pleased, made him Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; with Zhang Gun he jointly handled the crucial portfolios and drafted founding institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had long known his name, sent riders to seize him and bring him to the army gate; they talked, and the sovereign was pleased. He made Xuanbo gentleman at the yellow gate; with Zhang Gun he shared the weight of state and drafted the founding institutions.

sentences.zh: 時司馬德宗遣使來朝，太祖將報之，詔有司博議國號。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Dezong sent envoys; the Founding Emperor wished to reply and ordered the relevant offices to debate the national title broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dezong of Jin then sent envoys; the Founding Emperor meant to answer and ordered the ministries to debate the state's name at length.

sentences.zh: 玄伯議曰：「三皇五帝之立號也，或因所生之土，或即封國之名。

translations.literal: Xuanbo submitted an opinion: "The titles of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors either took the soil where they were born, or the name of the state they enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo argued: "The Three August Ones and Five Emperors took their titles either from the land that bore them or from the state that first enfeoffed them.

sentences.zh: 故虞夏商周始皆諸侯，及聖德既隆，萬國宗戴，稱號隨本，不復更立。

translations.literal: Thus Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou all began as feudal lords; when sagely virtue was ripe and all lands honored them, their titles followed their origins and they did not change again.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou all began as feudal lords; when sage virtue ripened and the world bowed to them, they kept the old name and did not choose another.

sentences.zh: 唯商人屢徙，改號曰殷，然猶兼行，不廢始基之稱。

translations.literal: Only the Shang people moved many times and changed the title to Yin, yet both names were used together without discarding the original founding designation.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Shang moved their seat again and again and added the name Yin, yet they kept both names and did not cast off the first.

sentences.zh: 故詩云『殷商之旅』，又云『天命玄鳥，降而生商，宅殷土茫茫』。

translations.literal: Hence the Odes say 'The hosts of Yin-Shang' and also 'Heaven commanded the dark bird, descended and gave birth to Shang, dwelling on vast Yin soil.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Odes sing of 'the hosts of Yin-Shang' and also 'Heaven ordered the dark bird to descend and bear Shang, dwelling on the vast Yin lands.'

sentences.zh: 此其義也。

translations.literal: That is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That is the point.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖以漢王定三秦，滅強楚，故遂以漢為號。

translations.literal: In former days Han Gaozu, as King of Han, settled the Three Qin and destroyed mighty Chu, and therefore took Han as his title.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu, while still king of Han, settled the Three Qin and broke mighty Chu, and so took Han for his dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 國家雖統北方廣漠之土，逮于陛下，應運龍飛，雖曰舊邦，受命惟新，是以登國之初，改代曰魏。

translations.literal: Though the state ruled the broad northern wastes, down to Your Majesty's rise on the dragon — though called an old domain, the mandate was fresh; therefore at the founding of the state Dai was changed to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Our house holds the wide northern wastes; down to Your Majesty's dragon rise the land is old but the mandate is new — at the founding of the state Dai was renamed Wei.

sentences.zh: 又慕容永亦奉進魏土。

translations.literal: Murong Yong also presented the Wei territory.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong too offered up the Wei lands.

sentences.zh: 夫『魏』者大名，神州之上國，斯乃革命之徵驗，利見之玄符也。

translations.literal: Wei is a great name, the upper state of the divine land — the token of revolution, the dark omen of favorable seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei is a great name, the foremost state of the sacred middle kingdom — the sign of revolution, the omen of a mandate fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜號為魏。

translations.literal: I foolishly think the title should be Wei.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge that the name be Wei.

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founding Emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 於是四方賓王之貢，咸稱大魏矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribute of guest kings from the four directions all called the state Great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute from the four quarters hailed the state as Great Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸鄴，歷問故事於玄伯，應對若流，太祖善之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor visited Ye, he questioned Xuanbo on old stories at length; his answers flowed like water and the Founding Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye the Founding Emperor questioned him at length on ancient matters; his answers ran clear as water and won the sovereign's praise.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還京師，次於恒嶺。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital it halted at Heng Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to the capital the court halted at Heng Ridge.

sentences.zh: 太祖親登山頂，撫慰新民，適遇玄伯扶老母登嶺，太祖嘉之，賜以牛米。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor personally ascended the mountaintop to comfort the newly moved people; he happened upon Xuanbo supporting his aged mother up the ridge; the Founding Emperor commended this and gave him grain and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor climbed the ridge to comfort the newly resettled people and came upon Xuanbo helping his aged mother up the slope; he commended him and gave him grain and cattle.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸徙人不能自進者，給以車牛。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered that among the relocated who could not advance on their own, carriages and oxen be provided.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered carriages and oxen for any migrant who could not walk the road on his own.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 命有司制官爵，撰朝儀，協音樂，定律令，申科禁，玄伯總而裁之，以為永式。

translations.literal: He was ordered to devise ranks and offices, compile court ceremony, harmonize music, fix laws and orders, clarify prohibitions and penalties — Xuanbo oversaw and trimmed all of it and made it the enduring pattern.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged to shape ranks and offices, draft court ritual, tune the music, set laws and bans — Xuanbo trimmed the whole and fixed it as lasting pattern.

sentences.zh: 及置八部大夫以擬八坐，玄伯通署三十六曹，如令僕統事，深為太祖所任。

translations.literal: When eight ministry grandees were set up to mirror the eight excellencies, Xuanbo broadly supervised thirty-six bureaus like a chief steward directing affairs — deeply trusted by the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When eight ministry grandees were set to mirror the eight excellencies, Xuanbo oversaw thirty-six bureaus at large, like a chief steward running the house, and the Founding Emperor relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: His power tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: His influence bent the court.

sentences.zh: 而儉約自居，不營產業，家徒四壁；

translations.literal: Yet he lived frugally himself, did not seek wealth — bare walls at home;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lived sparely and sought no fortune — bare walls at home;

sentences.zh: 出無車乘，朝晡步上；

translations.literal: going out he had no carriage; morning and evening he walked to court;
translations.idiomatic: he kept no carriage and walked to court morning and night;

sentences.zh: 母年七十，供養無重膳。

translations.literal: his mother was seventy; he could not supply her with rich meals.
translations.idiomatic: his mother was seventy and he could not set a full table before her.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗使人密察，聞而益重之，厚加饋賜。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor once had someone observe him secretly; hearing this he valued him all the more and sent generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor once had him watched in secret; learning this he prized him the more and sent rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 時人亦或譏其過約，而玄伯為之踰甚。

translations.literal: Some in the time also mocked his excessive austerity, yet Xuanbo only grew stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked his harsh thrift, but Xuanbo only grew stricter.

sentences.zh: 太祖常引問古今舊事，王者制度，治世之則。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor often questioned him on old stories and institutions of enlightened rulers, the rules for governing an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor often asked him of ancient ways, of enlightened kings and their institutions, of how to settle an age.

sentences.zh: 玄伯陳古人制作之體，及明君賢臣，往代廢興之由，甚合上意。

translations.literal: Xuanbo set forth how the ancients fashioned institutions and how enlightened rulers and worthy ministers rose and fell in each age — greatly matching the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo laid out how the ancients built government, how sage rulers and worthy ministers rose and fell — and the sovereign's mind was well met.

sentences.zh: 未嘗謇諤忤旨，亦不諂諛苟容。

translations.literal: He never bluntly opposed orders, nor did he flatter for easy favor.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke blunt contradiction, nor fawned for easy grace.

sentences.zh: 及太祖季年，大臣多犯威怒，玄伯獨無譴者，由於此也。

translations.literal: In the Founding Emperor's last years many great ministers drew wrath; Xuanbo alone was never reproached — for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the Founding Emperor's last years many great ministers drew rebuke; Xuanbo alone was never faulted — and that is why.

sentences.zh: 太祖曾引玄伯講漢書，至婁敬說漢祖欲以魯元公主妻匈奴，善之，嗟歎者良久。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor once had Xuanbo expound the Han Records; reaching Lou Jing's advice that Han Zu wanted to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu, he was pleased and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Founding Emperor had him expound the Han Records; when they came to Lou Jing urging Gaozu to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu, he was pleased and sighed long.

sentences.zh: 是以諸公主皆釐降于賓附之國，朝臣子弟，雖名族美彥，不得尚焉。

translations.literal: Hence all princesses were married down into tributary states; sons of court ministers, though of noble houses and fine repute, could not marry them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth princesses were sent in marriage to tributary states, and even sons of great houses of shining name could not wed them.

sentences.zh: 尚書職罷，賜玄伯爵白馬侯，加周兵將軍，與舊功臣庾岳、奚斤等同班，而信寵過之。

translations.literal: When the post of Director of the Masters of Writing was abolished he enfeoffed Xuanbo as Marquis of Baima and added the post General of Elite Troops of Zhou, ranking with old meritocrats Yu Yue and Xi Jin and the like — yet trust and favor passed beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: When the directorate of the masters of writing was abolished he enfeoffed Xuanbo as Marquis of Baima and made him general of elite troops of Zhou, ranking with old meritocrats Yu Yue and Xi Jin — yet favor ran deeper still.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，太宗未即位，清河王紹聞人心不安，大出財帛班賜朝士。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor died and Emperor Taizong had not yet taken the throne, Prince of Qinghe Shao heard hearts were uneasy and distributed wealth and silks broadly among court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor died and Taizong had not yet been enthroned, Prince of Qinghe Shao, sensing unrest, scattered wealth and silk among the court.

sentences.zh: 玄伯獨不受。

translations.literal: Xuanbo alone would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo alone refused.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，命玄伯居門下，虛己訪問，以不受紹財帛，特賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he ordered Xuanbo to remain at the Gate Department, visited him humbly for counsel; because he had not taken Shao's gifts, he was specially granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he kept Xuanbo at the gate department and sought his counsel with open humility; because he had refused Shao's gifts, he was specially granted two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩已下咸愧焉。

translations.literal: Changsun Song and those below were all ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song and the rest were shamed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使者巡行郡國，糾察守宰不如法者，令玄伯與宜都公穆觀等按之，太宗稱其平當。

translations.literal: An edict sent envoys to tour commanderies and kingdoms, investigating administrators who did not follow the law; Xuanbo was ordered with Duke of Yidu Mu Guan and others to conduct the review; Taizong praised their fairness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent envoys through commanderies and kingdoms to probe lawless administrators; Xuanbo was ordered with Duke of Yidu Mu Guan and others to judge them, and Taizong praised their fairness.

sentences.zh: 又詔玄伯與長孫嵩等坐朝堂，決刑獄。

translations.literal: Again he ordered Xuanbo with Changsun Song and others to sit in the Hall of Court and decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Again he ordered Xuanbo with Changsun Song and others to sit in the hall of court and decide criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 太宗以郡國豪右，大為民蠹，乃優詔徵之，民多戀本，而長吏逼遣。

translations.literal: Taizong, because powerful magnates of commanderies and kingdoms greatly harmed the people, issued a gracious edict summoning them; many clung to their native places while local chiefs forced them away.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, seeing that great clans in the commanderies preyed on the people, issued a gracious summons to bring them to court; many clung to home while their magistrates drove them on.

sentences.zh: 於是輕薄少年，因相扇動，所在聚結。

translations.literal: Therefore frivolous youths stirred one another and gathered wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: Then idle young men stirred one another and gathered wherever they could.

sentences.zh: 西河、建興盜賊並起，守宰討之不能禁。

translations.literal: Bandits rose together in Xihe and Jianxing; local chiefs could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands rose in Xihe and Jianxing, and local chiefs could not put them down.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃引玄伯及北新侯安同、壽光侯叔孫建、元城侯元屈等問曰：「前以兇俠亂民，故徵之京師，而守宰失於綏撫，令有逃竄。

translations.literal: Taizong therefore summoned Xuanbo, Duke of Beixin An Tong, Marquis of Shouguang Sun Jian, Marquis of Yuancheng Yuan Qu and asked: "Earlier because violent ruffians disturbed the people we summoned them to the capital, yet the administrators failed in soothing them and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then called Xuanbo, Duke of Beixin An Tong, Marquis of Shouguang Sun Jian, and Marquis of Yuancheng Yuan Qu and asked: "We summoned violent men to the capital because they troubled the people, yet the magistrates failed to soothe them and many fled.

sentences.zh: 今犯者已多，不可悉誅，朕欲大赦以紓之，卿等以為何如？

translations.literal: Now offenders are many and cannot all be executed; I wish a great amnesty to relieve this — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Now the guilty are many and cannot all be killed; I wish a great amnesty to ease the matter — what do you say?

sentences.zh: 」屈對曰：「民逃不罪而反赦之，似若有求於下，不如先誅首惡，赦其黨類。

translations.literal: " Qu replied: "If people flee without crime yet you pardon anyway, it seems as though the throne is begging those below; better first execute the chief evildoers and pardon their followers.
translations.idiomatic: " Qu answered: "If men flee though guiltless and you pardon all the same, it will look as if the throne begs its subjects. Better execute the ringleaders first and pardon the rest.

sentences.zh: 」玄伯曰：「王者治天下，以安民為本，何能顧小曲直也。

translations.literal: " Xuanbo said: "A king governs all under Heaven with settling the people as root — how can he mind small bends of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanbo said: "A king rules the world with the people's peace as his root — he cannot fuss over small twists of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 譬琴瑟不調，必改而更張；

translations.literal: If zither and lute are out of tune, they must be restrung;
translations.idiomatic: When zither and lute are out of tune, they must be restrung;

sentences.zh: 法度不平，亦須蕩而更制。

translations.literal: if laws are uneven, they must be swept away and remade.
translations.idiomatic: when laws lean awry, they must be cleared away and set anew.

sentences.zh: 夫赦雖非正道，而可以權行，自秦漢以來，莫不相踵。

translations.literal: Amnesty is not the straight path, yet may be used as expedient; from Qin and Han onward none failed to follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is not the straight road, yet may serve as expedient; from Qin and Han on none failed to use it in turn.

sentences.zh: 屈言先誅後赦，會於不能兩去，孰與一行便定。

translations.literal: Qu's words — execute first then pardon — meet at being unable to do both; which is better than one act to settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's plan — kill first, pardon after — cannot do both; better one stroke to settle the affair.

sentences.zh: 若其赦而不改者，誅之不晚。

translations.literal: If after pardon they still do not reform, execution is not too late.
translations.idiomatic: If after pardon they still do not mend, execution will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」太宗從之。

translations.literal: " Taizong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 神瑞初，詔玄伯與南平公嵩等坐止車門右，聽理萬機事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenrui era he ordered Xuanbo with Duke of Nanping Song and others to sit to the right of the carriage-halting gate and manage myriad state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenrui era he ordered Xuanbo with Duke of Nanping Song and others to sit right of the carriage-halting gate and handle the weight of state.

sentences.zh: 并州胡數萬家南掠河內，遣將軍公孫表等率師討之，敗績。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bingzhou raided south into the interior riverlands; General Gongsun Biao and others led troops against them and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bingzhou raided south into the inner riverlands; General Gongsun Biao and others marched against them and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 太宗問羣臣曰：「胡寇縱暴，人眾不少，表等已不能制。

translations.literal: Taizong asked the assembled ministers: "The Hu raiders run wild and their numbers are not few; Biao and the rest cannot control them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked the ministers: "The Hu run wild and their numbers are great; Biao and his command cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 若不早誅，則良民大受其禍。

translations.literal: If we do not strike early the good people will suffer great harm.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not strike soon the good people will suffer deeply.

sentences.zh: 今既盛秋，不可為此小盜，而復興眾以廢民業。

translations.literal: Now it is deep autumn — we cannot for small bandits again raise hosts and abandon the people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is deep autumn — we cannot for small bandits raise great armies again and ruin the people's harvest.

sentences.zh: 將若之何？

translations.literal: What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done? (record).

sentences.zh: 」玄伯對曰：「表等諸軍，不為不足，但失於處分，故使小盜假息耳。

translations.literal: " Xuanbo replied: "Biao's armies are not insufficient, but they failed in disposition, so the small bandits gained a breathing space.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanbo answered: "Biao's forces were not too few; they failed in deployment, and so the small bandits caught their breath.

sentences.zh: 胡眾雖盛，而無猛健主將，所謂千奴共一膽也。

translations.literal: Though the Hu masses are large they have no fierce chief commander — as the saying goes, a thousand slaves share one gallbladder.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Hu are many, they have no bold master to lead them — as the proverb says, a thousand slaves share one gut.

sentences.zh: 宜得大將軍為胡所服信者，將數百騎，就攝表軍以討之，賊聞之，必望風震怖。

translations.literal: One should choose a great general whom the Hu obey and trust, take several hundred horsemen, go to take command of Biao's army and subdue them — when the bandits hear of it they will surely quake at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Pick a great general the Hu fear and obey, give him a few hundred riders, and send him to take Biao's army in hand — when the bandits hear of it they will break at the mere rumor.

sentences.zh: 壽光侯建，前在并州，號為威猛，胡醜畏服，諸將莫及。

translations.literal: Marquis of Shouguang Jian, formerly in Bingzhou, was famed as fierce and martial; the Hu feared and submitted to him, and no general could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Shouguang Sun Jian had once held Bingzhou, famed as fierce and martial; the Hu feared him and bowed, and no general could stand beside him.

sentences.zh: 」太宗從之，遂平胡寇。

translations.literal: " Taizong followed this and thereupon pacified the Hu raiders.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong took his counsel and pacified the Hu raiders.

sentences.zh: 尋拜天部大人，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief of the Celestial Department and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief of the celestial department and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 泰常三年夏，玄伯病篤，太宗遣侍中宜都公穆觀就受遺言，更遣侍臣問疾，一夜數返。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Taichang, Xuanbo's illness grew grave; Taizong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Duke of Yidu Mu Guan to receive his last words, and again sent court attendants to inquire after his health — several times in one night.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taichang, summer, Xuanbo's illness turned grave; Taizong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Duke of Yidu Mu Guan to take his last words and sent court attendants to ask after him again and again through the night.

sentences.zh: 及卒，下詔痛惜，贈司空，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: When he died, an edict mourned him deeply; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and titled Duke Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the throne mourned him in edict, posthumously made him minister of works, and titled him Duke Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral followed wholly the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

sentences.zh: 詔羣臣及附國渠帥皆會葬，自親王以外，盡令拜送。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all ministers and attached-state chieftains to attend the burial; except for princes of the blood, all were made to bow and escort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gathered every minister and attached-state chieftain to the burial; save for princes of the blood, all were made to bow and escort the bier.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖追錄先朝功臣，以玄伯配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Emperor Gaozu, recording meritorious ministers of the former court, had Xuanbo receive joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era Emperor Gaozu, recording ministers of the former court, had Xuanbo given joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 玄伯自非朝廷文誥，四方書檄，初不染翰，故世無遺文。

translations.literal: Unless for court documents of the throne or letters to the four directions, Xuanbo never touched the brush — hence no writings survive in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Unless for court edicts or letters to the four quarters, Xuanbo never took up the brush — and so no writings of his survive.

sentences.zh: 尤善草隸行押之書，為世摹楷。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script — models for the age.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script, and the age copied him as its model.

sentences.zh: 玄伯祖悅與范陽盧諶，並以博藝著名。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang Lu Chen were both famed for broad arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were both famed for wide learning in the arts.

sentences.zh: 諶法鍾繇，悅法衞瓘，而俱習索靖之草，皆盡其妙。

translations.literal: Chen learned from Zhong You, Yue from Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive — each attaining the utmost subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Chen took Zhong You as his model, Yue took Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive until each reached its utmost subtlety.

sentences.zh: 諶傳子偃，偃傳子邈；

translations.literal: Chen passed it to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;
translations.idiomatic: Chen passed the art to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;

sentences.zh: 悅傳子潛，潛傳玄伯。

translations.literal: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 世不替業。

translations.literal: The craft was never broken through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: The craft never failed from father to son.

sentences.zh: 故魏初重崔盧之書。

translations.literal: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were prized.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were held in highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 又玄伯之行押，特盡精巧，而不見遺迹。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's running-draft script too was especially refined and ingenious, yet no traces survive.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo's running-draft hand too was wrought to rare refinement, yet no trace of it remains.

sentences.zh: 子浩，襲爵，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Hao inherited the title; he is treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao inherited the title and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 次子簡，字沖亮，[5]一名覽。

translations.literal: The second son Jian, courtesy name Chongliang, [5] also called Lan.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Jian, courtesy name Chongliang,[5] was also called Lan.

sentences.zh: 好學，少以善書知名。

translations.literal: He loved learning and in youth was famed for fine calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and in youth was famed for fine calligraphy — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，[6]歷位中書侍郎、征虜將軍，爵五等侯，參著作事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Founding Emperor's reign, [6] he rose through posts to Secretariat Gentleman, General Who Campaigns the Barbarians, Five-Rank Marquis, and participated in compiling the dynastic record.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Founding Emperor's reign[6] he rose step by step to secretariat gentleman, general who campaigns the barbarians, five-rank marquis, and a post compiling the dynastic record.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 簡弟恬，字叔玄，小名白。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Tian, courtesy name Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Tian, courtesy name Shuxuan, childhood name Bai — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 歷給事中，賜爵繹幕子。

translations.literal: He rose through attendant at court audience and was granted the title Baron of Yimu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through attendant at court audience and was granted the title baron of Yimu.

sentences.zh: 出為上黨太守、平南將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Shangdang, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Shangdang, general who pacifies the south, and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進爵陽武侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Marquis of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 坐浩伏誅。

translations.literal: He was executed on account of Hao's crime.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed when Hao fell.

sentences.zh: 始玄伯因苻堅亂，欲避地江南，於泰山為張願所獲，本圖不遂，乃作詩以自傷，而不行於時，蓋懼罪也。

translations.literal: At first, because of the turmoil of Fu Jian, Xuanbo wished to flee south to the Yangtze; on Mount Tai he was seized by Zhang Yuan — his plan failed, so he wrote a poem to wound himself, yet did not circulate it in his time, fearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, in the chaos of Fu Jian's fall, Xuanbo meant to flee south across the Yangtze; on Mount Tai Zhang Yuan seized him. The plan failed, and he wrote a poem to grieve himself, yet dared not let it circulate, fearing blame.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，中書侍郎高允受敕收浩家，始見此詩。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun received an edict to seize Hao's household and first saw this poem.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, secretariat gentleman Gao Yun, ordered to seize Hao's household, first saw this poem.

sentences.zh: 允知其意，允孫綽錄於允集。

translations.literal: Yun understood its intent; Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Yun knew what it meant; Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.

sentences.zh: 始玄伯父潛為兄渾誄手筆草本，[7]延昌初，著作佐郎王遵業買書於市而遇得之。

translations.literal: At first Xuanbo's uncle Qian had written the draft eulogy for his brother Hun in his own hand; [7] in the beginning of the Yanchang era, Assistant in the Office for Compiling the Dynastic Record Wang Zunye bought books in the market and came upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Xuanbo's uncle Qian had penned in his own hand the draft eulogy for his brother Hun;[7] at the opening of the Yanchang era, assistant in the office for compiling the dynastic record Wang Zunye bought books in the market and found it.

sentences.zh: 計誄至今，將二百載，寶其書迹，深藏祕之。

translations.literal: Counting from the eulogy to the present, nearly two hundred years had passed; he treasured the writing and kept it hidden deep.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly two hundred years had passed since the eulogy was written; he treasured the script and hid it away.

sentences.zh: 武定中，遵業子松年以遺黃門郎崔季舒，人多摹搨之。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Zunye's son Songnian gave it to Attendant at the Yellow Gate Cui Jishu, and many copied it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era Zunye's son Songnian gave it to attendant at the yellow gate Cui Jishu, and many took copies.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫姚元標以工書知名於時，見潛書，謂為過於己也。

translations.literal: Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall Yao Yuanbiao, famed in the time for skill in calligraphy, saw Qian's writing and said it surpassed his own.
translations.idiomatic: Left grand master of the bright hall Yao Yuanbiao, famed in his day for calligraphy, saw Qian's hand and said it surpassed his own.

sentences.zh: 玄伯弟徽，字玄猷。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's younger brother Hui, courtesy name Xuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo's younger brother Hui, courtesy name Xuanyou — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 少有文才，與勃海高演俱知名。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary talent and was famed together with Bohai Gao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had literary gift and shared renown with Bohai's Gao Yan.

sentences.zh: 初徵相州別駕、中書侍郎，稍遷祕書監，賜爵貝丘侯，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned as Vice Prefect of Xiangzhou and Secretariat Gentleman; he was gradually moved to Director of the Secretariat, granted Marquis of Beiqiu, and made Dragon-Charging General.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was summoned as vice prefect of Xiangzhou and secretariat gentleman; he rose by degrees to director of the secretariat, was granted marquis of Beiqiu, and made dragon-charging general.

sentences.zh: 樂安王範鎮長安，世祖以範年少，而三秦民夷，恃險多變，乃選忠清舊德之士，與範俱鎮。

translations.literal: Prince of Le'an Fan was stationed at Chang'an; Emperor Shizu, because Fan was young and the people of the three Qin — Han and alien alike — relied on perilous terrain and were prone to change, chose men of old loyalty and clear virtue to guard with him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Le'an Fan held Chang'an; Emperor Shizu, seeing Fan was young and that Han and alien alike in the three Qin leaned on rough country and were quick to turn, chose men of old loyalty and clear virtue to stand guard with him.

sentences.zh: 以徽為散騎常侍、督雍涇梁秦四州諸軍事、平西將軍、副將，行樂安王傅，進爵濟南公。

translations.literal: Hui was made Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, overseer of military affairs of Yong, Jing, Liang, and Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, deputy commander, acting Tutor to the Prince of Le'an, and advanced to Duke of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was made regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, overseer of military affairs in Yong, Jing, Liang, and Qin, general who pacifies the west, deputy commander, acting tutor to the prince of Le'an, and raised to duke of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 徽為政務存大體，不親小事。

translations.literal: In government he kept to the great outline and did not busy himself with small matters.
translations.idiomatic: In office he kept to the great outline and did not fuss over small things.

sentences.zh: 性好人倫。

translations.literal: By nature he loved human relations.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved the weave of human ties.

sentences.zh: 引接賓客，或談及平生，或講論道義，誨誘後進，終日不止。

translations.literal: Receiving guests he might speak of days gone by or discourse on right conduct, instructing the young — all day without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he received guests he might speak of days gone by or argue the way of right, guiding the young without cease from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 以疾徵還京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness summoned him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 真君四年卒，諡曰元公。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhenjun, posthumously titled Duke Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenjun and was posthumously titled Duke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 士類無不歎惜。

translations.literal: Men of standing all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing all sighed for him.

sentences.zh: 時清河崔寬，字景仁。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Kuan of Qinghe, courtesy name Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Kuan of Qinghe, courtesy name Jingren — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 祖彤，隨晉南陽王保避地隴右，遂仕於沮渠、李暠。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong, following Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao, fled to Longyou and then served Juqu and Li Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong, following Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao, fled to Longyou and then served Juqu and Li Gao — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 父剖，字伯宗，每慷慨有懷東土，常歎曰：「風雨如晦，鷄鳴不已，吾所庶幾。

translations.literal: His father Pou, courtesy name Bozong, was often ardent with longing for the eastern lands and would sigh: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows unceasing — that is what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pou, courtesy name Bozong, burned with longing for the eastern lands and often sighed: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows without cease — that is what I hope for.

sentences.zh: 」及世祖西巡，剖乃總率同義，使寬送款。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizu toured west, Pou gathered those of shared intent and sent Kuan to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Shizu toured west, Pou gathered men of shared intent and sent Kuan to offer allegiance.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，拜寬威遠將軍、岐陽令，賜爵沂水男。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this, made Kuan General of Awesome Distance, Magistrate of Qiyang, and granted him Baron of Yishui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him, made Kuan general of awesome distance and magistrate of Qiyang, and granted him baron of Yishui.

sentences.zh: 遣使與寬俱西，撫慰初附。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to go west with Kuan and soothe the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy west with Kuan to soothe the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 徵剖詣京師，未至，病卒。

translations.literal: Pou was summoned to the capital but fell ill and died before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Pou was summoned to the capital but fell ill and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 高宗以剖誠著先朝，贈散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、涼州刺史、武陵公，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Pou's loyalty had shown in the former court, posthumously made him Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, General Who Stabilizes the West, Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Wuling, posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, because Pou's loyalty had shone in the former reign, posthumously made him regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, general who stabilizes the west, inspector of Liangzhou, duke of Wuling, with posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 寬還京，拜散騎侍郎、寧朔將軍、安國子。

translations.literal: Kuan returned to court and was made Secretariat Gentleman, General Who Pacifies the North, and Baron of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan returned to court as secretariat gentleman, general who pacifies the north, and baron of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為弘農太守。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out as administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初，寬之通款也，見司徒浩。

translations.literal: When Kuan first submitted allegiance he met Minister of Works Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuan first offered allegiance he met minister of works Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩與相齒次，厚存撫之。

translations.literal: Hao was near him in age and treated him with deep kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was near his age and treated him with deep kindness.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，以遠來疏族，獨得不坐。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, as a distant kinsman who had come from afar he alone was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, as a distant kinsman newly come from the west he alone escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 遂家于武城，居司空林舊墟，以一子繼浩弟覽妻封氏，[8]相奉如親。

translations.literal: He then made his home in Wucheng, dwelling on the old site of the Minister of Works' grove, and had one son inherit the wife of Hao's younger brother Lan, nee Feng, [8] — they supported one another as kin.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled in Wucheng on the old grove of the minister of works and had one son take as wife Hao's younger brother Lan's widow, nee Feng,[8] tending one another as kin.

sentences.zh: 寬後襲爵武陵公、鎮西將軍，拜陝城鎮將。

translations.literal: Later Kuan inherited the title Duke of Wuling and General Who Stabilizes the West and was made garrison commander of Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuan inherited duke of Wuling and general who stabilizes the west and was made garrison commander of Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 二崤地嶮，[9]民多寇劫。

translations.literal: The land of the two Xiao passes was perilous; [9] the people were much given to robbery.
translations.idiomatic: The two Xiao passes were steep country;[9] the people were much given to robbery.

sentences.zh: 寬性滑稽，誘接豪右、宿盜魁帥，與相交結，傾衿待遇，不逆微細。

translations.literal: Kuan was by nature witty; he drew in local magnates and chiefs of old bandits, befriended them, poured out his heart in treating them, and did not reject even small matters.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was witty by nature; he drew in local magnates and chiefs of old bandit bands, befriended them, poured out his heart, and did not spurn even small courtesies.

sentences.zh: 是以能得民庶忻心，莫不感其意氣。

translations.literal: Thus he could win the people's glad hearts — none failed to be moved by his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he won the people's glad hearts, and none failed to answer his spirit.

sentences.zh: 時官無祿力，唯取給於民。

translations.literal: At the time officials had no salary allotment and took their supply only from the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officials had no salary and lived only on what the people gave.

sentences.zh: 寬善撫納，招致禮遺，大有受取，而與之者無恨。

translations.literal: Kuan was skilled at soothing and drawing them in, inviting gifts of courtesy — he received much, yet those who gave bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was skilled at soothing them and drawing gifts of courtesy; he took much, yet those who gave bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 又弘農出漆蠟竹木之饒，路與南通，販貿來往。

translations.literal: Moreover Hongnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber, and the roads ran south in trade.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Hongnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber, and the roads ran south with merchants.

sentences.zh: 家產豐富，而百姓樂之。

translations.literal: His household grew wealthy, yet the common people were glad of it.
translations.idiomatic: His house grew rich, yet the common people were glad of it.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮之中，號為能政。

translations.literal: Among the garrisons he was called able in government.
translations.idiomatic: Among the garrisons he was called able in government — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 及解鎮還京，民多追戀，詣闕上章者三百餘人。

translations.literal: When he left the garrison and returned to the capital, many people followed in longing; more than three hundred went to the palace gates with memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the garrison for the capital, many followed in longing, and more than three hundred brought memorials to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 書奏，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When the memorials were submitted, Emperor Gaozu commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorials were read, Emperor Gaozu commended him.

sentences.zh: 延興二年卒，年六十三，遺命薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yanxing, aged sixty-three; he left orders for a plain burial, enshrouded in daily dress.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yanxing, aged sixty-three, leaving orders for a plain burial in the clothes he wore day to day.

sentences.zh: 長子敞，字公世，襲爵，例降為侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chang, courtesy name Gongshi, inherited the title; by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chang, courtesy name Gongshi, inherited the title; by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 自謁者僕射，出為平原相。

translations.literal: From Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Masters of Writing he went out as Chancellor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: From attendant-in-ordinary of the masters of writing he went out as chancellor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 敞性狷急，與刺史楊椿迭相表列，敞坐免官。

translations.literal: Chang was by nature harsh and impatient; he and Inspector Yang Chun repeatedly memorialized against each other, and Chang was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was harsh and impatient; he and inspector Yang Chun repeatedly denounced each other in memorials, and Chang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 弟朏之逆，敞為黃木軍主韓文殊所藏。

translations.literal: When his younger brother Fei rebelled, Chang was hidden by Huangmu Army Commander Han Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Fei rebelled, Chang was hidden by Huangmu army commander Han Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 其家悉見籍沒，唯敞妻李氏，以公主之甥，自隨奴婢田宅二百餘口得免。

translations.literal: His whole household was registered and confiscated; only Chang's wife, Lady Li, as a princess's niece, kept with her two hundred-odd slaves, fields, and houses and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His whole household was registered and seized; only Chang's wife, Lady Li, as a princess's niece, kept two hundred-odd slaves with their fields and houses and was spared.

sentences.zh: 正光中，普釋禁錮，敞復爵齊郡侯，拜龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era a general pardon lifted the ban; Chang recovered the title Marquis of Qijun and was made Dragon-Charging General and Palace Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era a general pardon lifted the ban; Chang recovered marquis of Qijun and was made dragon-charging general and palace scribe.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，趙郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was Administrator of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he was administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 敞弟鍾，字公祿，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Gonglu, was a court gentleman in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Gonglu, was a court gentleman in attendance — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 弟朏之逆，以出後被原。

translations.literal: When Fei rebelled, because he had been given in adoption to another line he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei rebelled, because he had been given in adoption to another line he was pardoned — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、國子博士、司徒右長史、征北將軍、金紫光祿大夫、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: He rose through Secretariat Gentleman, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Chief Rectifier of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through secretariat gentleman, erudite of the imperial academy, right chief clerk of the ministry of personnel, general who campaigns north, grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon, and chief rectifier of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 敞亡後，鍾貪其財物，誣敞息子積等三人，非兄之胤，辭訴累歲，人士嫉之。

translations.literal: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his goods and accused Chang's sons Ji and two others of not being his brother's seed; the suit dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his goods and accused Chang's sons Ji and two others of not being his brother's blood; the suit dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.

sentences.zh: 尒朱世隆為尚書令，奏除其官，終身不齒。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong as Director of the Masters of Writing memorialized to strip him of office — barred for life from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, as director of the masters of writing, memorialized to strip him of office and bar him for life from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 朏好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Fei loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fei loved learning and had literary gift.

sentences.zh: 歷治書侍御史、京兆王愉錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through Supervising Secretary and Recorder under Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through supervising secretary and recorder under Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

sentences.zh: 與愉同逆，伏法。

translations.literal: He joined Yu in rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yu in rebellion and was executed — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 衡弟恕，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother Shu was a Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's younger brother Shu was a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 又有崔模，字思範，魏中尉崔琰兄霸後也。

translations.literal: There was also Cui Mo, courtesy name Sifan, descendant of Wei's Commandant of the Capital Cui Yan's elder brother Ba.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cui Mo, courtesy name Sifan, descended from Wei's commandant of the capital Cui Yan's elder brother Ba.

sentences.zh: 父遵，慕容垂少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Junior Chamberlain under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun was junior chamberlain under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 叔父整，廣川太守。

translations.literal: His uncle Zheng was Administrator of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zheng was administrator of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 模，慕容熙末南渡河外，為劉裕滎陽太守，戍虎牢。

translations.literal: Mo, at the end of Murong Xi's reign, crossed south of the Yellow River and served Liu Yu as Administrator of Xingyang, garrisoning Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, at the end of Murong Xi's reign, crossed south of the Yellow River and served Liu Yu as administrator of Xingyang, garrisoning Hulao.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，平滑臺，模歸降。

translations.literal: In the Shenqi era Pingtai was pacified and Mo surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenqi era Pingtai was pacified and Mo surrendered — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 後賜爵武陵男，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was granted Baron of Wuling and made General Who Extends Far.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted baron of Wuling and made general who extends far.

sentences.zh: 始模在南妻張氏，有二子，沖智、季柔。

translations.literal: At first, while Mo was in the south, his wife Lady Zhang had two sons, Chongzhi and Jirou.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Mo was in the south, his wife Lady Zhang bore two sons, Chongzhi and Jirou.

sentences.zh: 模至京師，賜妻金氏，生子幼度。

translations.literal: When Mo reached the capital he was given Lady Jin as wife and she bore a son, Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo reached the capital he was given Lady Jin as wife, and she bore a son, Youdu.

sentences.zh: 沖智等以父隔遠，乃聚貨物，間託關境，規贖模歸。

translations.literal: Chongzhi and the others, because their father was far away, gathered goods and, through intermediaries at the border, plotted to ransom Mo home.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi and the others, their father far away, gathered goods and through men at the border plotted to ransom Mo home.

sentences.zh: 其母張氏每謂之曰：「汝父性懷，本自無決，必不能來也。

translations.literal: Their mother Lady Zhang would often say to them: "Your father's nature is timid at heart and by origin lacks resolve — he will surely not come.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother Lady Zhang would often tell them: "Your father's heart is timid and by nature he lacks resolve — he will surely not come."

sentences.zh: 」行人遂以財賄至都，當竊模還。

translations.literal: " The envoy then brought bribes to the capital, intending to steal Mo back.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy then brought bribes to the capital to steal Mo away.

sentences.zh: 模果顧念幼度等，指幼度謂行人曰：「吾何忍捨此輩，令坐致刑辱，當為爾取一人，使名位不減於我。

translations.literal: Mo indeed thought of Youdu and the others; he pointed at Youdu and said to the envoy: "How can I bear to abandon these and let them sit and bring punishment and shame upon themselves? I shall get one man for you so that rank and title do not fall below mine.
translations.idiomatic: Mo did think of Youdu and the rest; he pointed at Youdu and told the envoy: "How could I abandon them to sit and suffer shame and punishment? I will find you one man whose name and rank will not fall below mine.

sentences.zh: 」乃授以申謨。

translations.literal: " He then gave them Shen Mo.
translations.idiomatic: " He then handed over Shen Mo.

sentences.zh: 謨，劉義隆東郡太守，與朱脩之守滑臺，神䴥中，被執入國，俱得賜妻，生子靈度。

translations.literal: Mo was Liu Yilong's prefect of Dongjun; with Zhu Xiuzhi he defended Huatai. In the Shengui era he was captured and brought into the state; both received gifted wives, and Mo had a son, Lingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Mo had been Liu Yilong's prefect of Dongjun; with Zhu Xiuzhi he held Huatai. In the Shengui era both were taken captive and brought into Wei; each was given a wife by the court, and Mo had a son named Lingdu.

sentences.zh: 申謨聞此，乃棄妻子，走還江外。

translations.literal: When Shen Mo heard of this, he abandoned wife and children and fled back beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Mo heard of it, he abandoned wife and children and fled south of the river.

sentences.zh: 靈度刑為閹人。

translations.literal: Lingdu was punished by castration and made a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdu was castrated and made a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 模長者篤厚，不營榮利，頗為崔浩輕侮，而守志確然，不為浩屈。

translations.literal: Mo was a magnanimous elder, steadfast and generous; he did not seek glory or profit. Cui Hao often treated him lightly, yet he held his resolve firmly and would not yield to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was a generous, steadfast man who sought neither glory nor gain. Cui Hao often slighted him, yet he held firm to his principles and would not bend to Hao.

sentences.zh: 與崔賾相親，[11]往來如家。

translations.literal: He was close to Cui Lin; [11] they came and went like members of one household.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Cui Lin; [11] they visited back and forth as though of one family.

sentences.zh: 和平中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Heping era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Heping era.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，幼度隨慕容白曜為將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Youdu followed Murong Baiyao as a general.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangxing, Youdu served under Murong Baiyao as a commander.

sentences.zh: 時季柔為崔道固長史，帶濟南太守。

translations.literal: At that time Jirou was Cui Daogu's chief clerk, concurrently holding the post of Jinan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jirou was chief clerk to Cui Daogu and also acted as prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 城將降，先馳馬赴白曜軍，幼度亦豫令左右覘迎之，而差互不相值，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: When the city was about to surrender, Jirou first galloped to Baiyao's army; Youdu also had his attendants watch to welcome him, but by mischance they did not meet, and Jirou was killed by disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to surrender, Jirou rode ahead to Baiyao's camp; Youdu too had men posted to meet him, but their paths missed and Jirou was killed in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 初，真君末，車駕南克鄒山，模兄協子邪利為劉義隆魯郡太守，以郡降，賜爵臨淄子，拜廣寧太守，卒於郡。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Zhenjun, the imperial carriage south conquered Zou Mountain. Mo's brother Xie's son Xieli was Liu Yilong's prefect of Lu commandery; he surrendered the commandery, was granted the title Marquis of Linzi, was appointed prefect of Guangning, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in late Zhenjun, the emperor marched south and took Zou Mountain. Xieli, son of Mo's brother Xie, was Liu Yilong's prefect of Lu; he surrendered the commandery, received the title Marquis of Linzi, was made prefect of Guangning, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 邪利二子。

translations.literal: Xieli had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli had two sons — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 懷順以父入國，故不出仕。

translations.literal: Huaishun, because his father had entered the state, therefore did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun, whose father had come into Wei, did not enter government service.

sentences.zh: 及國家克青州，懷順迎邪利喪，還葬青州。

translations.literal: When the state conquered Qingzhou, Huaishun met Xieli's coffin and returned to bury him in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Qingzhou, Huaishun brought Xieli's coffin home and buried him there.

sentences.zh: 次恩，累政州主簿，至刺史陸龍成時謀叛，聚城北高柳村，將攻州城，龍成討斬之。

translations.literal: The younger, Ci'en, through successive administrations served as the commandery chief clerk; under Inspector Lu Longcheng he plotted rebellion, gathered at Gaoliu village north of the city, and was about to attack the prefectural seat; Longcheng attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Ci'en rose through repeated terms as commandery chief clerk; under Inspector Lu Longcheng he rebelled, mustered men at Gaoliu north of the city, and was about to storm the prefectural seat when Longcheng attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 懷順與冲智子徽伯等俱奔江外。

translations.literal: Huaishun, with Chongzhi's son Huibo and others, all fled beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun fled south of the river with Chongzhi's son Huibo and others.

sentences.zh: 始邪利與二女俱入國，一女為張氏婦，一女為劉休賓妻，生子文華。

translations.literal: At first Xieli and two daughters all entered the state; one daughter was a Zhang wife, one was Liu Xiubin's wife, and bore a son, Wenhua.
translations.idiomatic: When Xieli first came into Wei, his two daughters came with him; one married into the Zhang house, one became Liu Xiubin's wife and bore a son named Wenhua.

sentences.zh: [12]邪利後生庶子法始。

translations.literal: [12] Xieli later had a concubine-born son, Fashi.
translations.idiomatic: [12] Xieli later had a son by a concubine, Fashi.

sentences.zh: 邪利亡後，二女侮法始庶孽，常欲令文華襲外祖爵臨淄子。

translations.literal: After Xieli died, the two daughters insulted Fashi as a base-born son and often wished to have Wenhua inherit his maternal grandfather's title, Marquis of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xieli's death the two daughters belittled the concubine-born Fashi and kept pressing for Wenhua to inherit their grandfather's title of Marquis of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 法始恨忿，無所不為。

translations.literal: Fashi hated this and, in his resentment, did everything.
translations.idiomatic: Fashi burned with resentment and stopped at nothing.

sentences.zh: 後懷順歸化迎喪，始與法始相見。

translations.literal: Later, when Huaishun submitted and came to welcome the coffin, he first met Fashi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaishun later returned to Wei to bring back the coffin, he and Fashi met for the first time.

sentences.zh: 未幾，法始得襲爵，傳至孫延族，正光中，為冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Before long Fashi inherited the title; it passed to his grandson Yanzu, who in the Zhengguang era was Champion General and Palace Scattered Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fashi succeeded to the title; the line reached his grandson Yanzu, who in the Zhengguang era was champion general and palace scattered grandee.

sentences.zh: 季柔孫睦，正光三年，自郁州歸降。

translations.literal: Jirou's grandson Mu, in Zhengguang year 3, returned from Yuzhou and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jirou's grandson Mu, in the third year of Zhengguang, came back from Yuzhou and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 模孫景茂，冀州別駕、青州長史、隨郡太守、武城男。

translations.literal: Mo's grandson Jingmao was vice-prefect of Jizhou, chief clerk of Qingzhou, prefect of Suijun, and Baron of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's grandson Jingmao served as vice-prefect of Jizhou, chief clerk of Qingzhou, prefect of Suijun, and Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 景茂子彥遠，襲。

translations.literal: Jingmao's son Yanyuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao's son Yanyuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，北徐州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was vice marshal of northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was vice marshal of northern Xuzhou — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 始睦來降也，[13]與高陵張炅、郭縕俱至。

translations.literal: When Mu first came to surrender, [13] he arrived together with Zhang Ling of Gaoling and Guo Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu first surrendered, [13] he came with Zhang Ling of Gaoling and Guo Yun.

sentences.zh: 陵，蕭寶夤西討開府西閣祭酒，寶夤反，陵其黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Ling was libationer of the western pavilion in Xiao Baoyin's western-campaign opening office; when Baoyin rebelled, Ling was his yellow-gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ling had been western-pavilion libationer on Xiao Baoyin's western campaign staff; when Baoyin rebelled, Ling became his yellow-gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 關中平，還洛，歷尚書郎、定州別駕。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was pacified he returned to Luoyang, passing through the posts of palace gentleman and vice-prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanzhong was pacified he returned to Luoyang and served as palace gentleman and vice-prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王作相，以陵頗有文學，引參賓客。

translations.literal: When Duke Wen of Qi became chancellor, because Ling had considerable literary learning, he drew him in as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen of Qi took power as chancellor, he took Ling into his entourage for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 終於征南將軍、司空長史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as General Who Pacifies the South and chief clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as general who pacifies the south and chief clerk of the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、大司農卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Minister of Grand Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand general of agile cavalry and minister of grand granaries.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，有崔道固，字季堅，琰八世孫也。

translations.literal: In Xianzu's time there was Cui Daogu, styled Jijian, an eighth-generation descendant of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzu's reign there was Cui Daogu, styled Jijian, eighth in descent from Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖瓊，慕容垂車騎屬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiong was chariot-and-horse attache to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong was chariot-and-horse attache to Murong Chui — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 父輯，南徙青州，為泰山太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji moved south to Qingzhou and became prefect of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji moved south to Qingzhou and served as prefect of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 道固賤出，嫡母兄攸之、目連等輕侮之。

translations.literal: Daogu was born of a low-ranked mother; his elder half-brothers Youzhi, Mulian, and others treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was a son by a concubine; his elder half-brothers Youzhi, Mulian, and the rest looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 輯謂攸之曰：「此兒姿識如此，或能興人門戶，汝等何以輕之？
