translations.literal: Ji said to Youzhi: "This boy's gifts and insight are such that he may yet raise our clan's standing — why do you slight him?
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Youzhi: "This boy's talent and judgment are such that he may yet lift our house — why do you treat him so lightly?

sentences.zh: 」攸之等遇之彌薄，略無兄弟之禮。

translations.literal: " Youzhi and the others treated him even more thinly, with scarcely any brotherly courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " Youzhi and the others treated him all the more coldly, with hardly a trace of brotherly regard.

sentences.zh: 時劉義隆子駿為徐兗二州刺史，得辟他州民為從事。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yilong's son Jun was inspector of Xu and Yan provinces and could recruit men of other provinces as staff attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yilong's son Jun held Xu and Yan provinces and could take men from other regions onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 輯乃資給道固，令其南仕。

translations.literal: Ji then provided funds for Daogu and had him go south to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Ji supplied Daogu with funds and sent him south to enter service.

sentences.zh: 既至彭城，駿以為從事。

translations.literal: When he reached Pengcheng, Jun made him a staff attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Pengcheng, Jun made him a staff attendant.

sentences.zh: 道固美形容，善舉止，便弓馬，好武事，駿稍嘉之。

translations.literal: Daogu had handsome features and fine bearing; he was skilled at bow and horse and loved military affairs, and Jun gradually praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was handsome and carried himself well, skilled in archery and horsemanship and fond of military affairs; Jun came to think well of him.

sentences.zh: 會青州刺史新除，過彭城，駿謂之曰：「崔道固人身如此，豈可為寒士至老乎？

translations.literal: When the newly appointed Qingzhou inspector passed through Pengcheng, Jun said to him: "Cui Daogu's person is such — how can he remain a cold scholar to the end of his days?
translations.idiomatic: As the new Qingzhou inspector passed through Pengcheng, Jun said to him: "A man like Cui Daogu — how can he waste his life as a nobody?

sentences.zh: 而世人以其偏庶，便相陵侮，可為歎息。

translations.literal: Yet the world, because he is a partial bastard, bullies him — it is something to lament.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the world, seeing him as a concubine's son, heaps insult on him — it is a pity.

sentences.zh: 」青州刺史至州，辟為主簿，轉治中。

translations.literal: " When the Qingzhou inspector reached his post, he recruited Daogu as chief clerk and later promoted him to chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Qingzhou inspector took office, he made Daogu chief clerk and later chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 後為義隆諸子參軍事，被遣向青州募人。

translations.literal: Later he was a staff officer to Yilong's sons and was sent to Qingzhou to recruit men.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the staffs of Yilong's sons and was sent to Qingzhou to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 長史已下皆詣道固，道固諸兄等逼道固所生母自致酒炙於客前。

translations.literal: The chief clerk down all went to Daogu's place; Daogu's brothers forced Daogu's birth mother to bring wine and food before the guests herself.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk and all below came to Daogu; his brothers forced his birth mother to serve wine and food to the guests with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 道固驚起接取，謂客曰：「家無人力，老親自執劬勞。

translations.literal: Daogu started up in alarm and took them from her, saying to the guests: "Our house has no servants; the old mother herself performs toilsome labor.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu started up in alarm and took the tray from her, telling the guests: "We have no household staff; my mother herself does the hard work.

sentences.zh: 」諸客皆知其兄弟所作，咸起拜謝其母。

translations.literal: " All the guests knew it was his brothers' doing and all rose to bow and thank his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " The guests all knew what his brothers had done and rose to bow to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母謂道固曰：「我賤不足以報貴賓，汝宜答拜。

translations.literal: The mother said to Daogu: "I am too lowly to repay honored guests — you should return the bow for me.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told Daogu: "I am not fit to receive such guests — you must bow in my place.

sentences.zh: 」諸客皆歎美道固母子，賤其諸兄。

translations.literal: " All the guests sighed in admiration at Daogu and his mother and despised his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: " The guests praised mother and son and despised the brothers.

sentences.zh: 後為寧朔將軍、冀州刺史，移鎮歷城。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Calms the North and Inspector of Jizhou and moved his garrison to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general who calms the north and inspector of Jizhou and shifted his command to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 劉彧既殺子業自立，徐州刺史薛安都與道固等舉兵推立子業弟子勛。

translations.literal: After Liu Yu killed Ziye and established himself, Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu, with Daogu and others, raised troops to install Ziye's nephew Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu killed Ziye and seized the throne, Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu joined Daogu and others in raising troops for Ziye's nephew Zixun.

sentences.zh: 子勛敗，乃遣表歸誠，顯祖以為安南將軍、南冀州刺史、清河公。

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated, Daogu sent a memorial of submission; Xianzu made him General Who Pacifies the South, southern Jizhou inspector, and Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun fell, Daogu sent in his allegiance; Xianzu made him general who pacifies the south, southern Jizhou inspector, and Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 劉彧遣說道固，以為前將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent envoys to win Daogu over, making him former general and Xuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent envoys to win him back, offering the posts of former general and Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 復叛受彧命。

translations.literal: He rebelled again and accepted Yu's commission.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled again and took Yu's orders.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，顯祖詔征南大將軍慕容白曜固築長圍以守之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Xianzu ordered Southern Campaign Grand General Murong Baiyao to build a tight encirclement and hold him there.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangxing, Xianzu ordered southern campaign grand general Murong Baiyao to tighten the siege around him.

sentences.zh: 及白曜攻其城東郭，道固面縛請罪，表曰：「臣資生南境，限隔大化，本朝不以卑末，委授藩任。

translations.literal: When Baiyao attacked the eastern outer wall of the city, Daogu bound himself and asked guilt, submitting a memorial that said: "I was born in the southern realm, cut off by great transformation; our court, not because of my low origin, entrusted me with a border command.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiyao assaulted the eastern suburb of the city, Daogu came out bound and pleaded guilty, writing: "I was born in the south, cut off from your transforming rule; yet your court, though I was low-born, gave me a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 而劉氏蕭牆內侮，懼貽大戮，前遣崔啟之奉表歸誠，幸蒙陛下過垂矜納，并賜爵寵，慶佩罔極，應奔闕庭。

translations.literal: But the Liu house had inner strife and I feared great punishment; I formerly sent Cui Qizhi with a memorial of submission and was fortunate that Your Majesty overmuch showed pity and acceptance, also granting title and favor — boundless rejoicing; I should have rushed to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu house turned on itself I feared execution; I sent Cui Qizhi with a memorial of surrender, and Your Majesty in extraordinary mercy accepted me and granted rank — joy beyond measure — and I should have hurried to court.

sentences.zh: 但劉彧尋續遣使，恕臣百死。

translations.literal: But Liu Yu soon again sent envoys, pardoning my hundred deaths.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Yu soon sent envoys again and spared me from a hundred deaths.

sentences.zh: 愚以世奉劉氏，深愆蒙宥，若猶違背，則是不忠於本朝，而欲求忠於大魏。

translations.literal: I foolishly thought that, since my house had served Liu for generations and had already deeply offended yet received pardon, to rebel again would be unfaithful to our court while seeking faithfulness to Great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Foolishly I reasoned that, having served Liu for generations and already been spared after grave offense, to rebel again would dishonor your court even as I sought favor from Great Wei.

sentences.zh: 雖曰希生，懼大魏之所不許。

translations.literal: Though one might call it wishing to live, I feared Great Wei would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: One may call that clinging to life, but I feared Wei would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 是用迷回，孤負天日，冒萬死之艱，固執拒守。

translations.literal: Therefore I was confused and turned back, alone betraying heaven and sun, braving ten-thousand deaths, stubbornly holding and resisting.
translations.idiomatic: So I wavered, turned my back on heaven's light, risked death ten thousand times, and held the city in stubborn defiance.

sentences.zh: 僕臣白曜，[14]振曜威靈，漸經二載，大將臨城，以今月十四日，臣東郭失守，於臣款彧之誠，庶可以彰於大魏矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Baiyao, [14] shook and displayed awesome spirit; gradually over two years the great general came to the city — on the fourteenth day of this month my eastern outer wall was lost — regarding my sincere intent toward Yu, perhaps it can be made manifest to Great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Baiyao, [14] has shown his awful might; for nearly two years his great army has sat before the walls — on the fourteenth of this month my eastern suburb fell — and by that, I trust, my loyalty to Liu Yu stands clear before Great Wei.

sentences.zh: 臣勢窮力屈，以十七日面縛請罪，白曜奉宣皇恩，恕臣生命。

translations.literal: My situation was exhausted and my strength spent; on the seventeenth I bound myself and asked guilt, and Baiyao carried out the imperial grace and pardoned my life.
translations.idiomatic: My strength was spent; on the seventeenth I came out bound to plead guilty, and Baiyao, executing imperial grace, spared my life.

sentences.zh: 斯實陛下起臣死尸，肉臣朽骨，天地造物所不能行，而陛下育之。

translations.literal: This truly is Your Majesty raising me from a corpse and fleshing my rotten bones — what heaven and earth in creating could not do, Your Majesty has done.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly Your Majesty raising the dead and putting flesh on dry bones — what heaven and earth could not do, Your Majesty has done.

sentences.zh: 雖虞舜之貸有苗，姬文之宥崇壘，方之聖澤，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Though Yu Shun's lending to You Miao and Ji Wen's pardoning of Chong's fortress — compared with sage grace, they are not enough to illustrate.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yu Shun's sparing of You Miao and King Wen's pardon at Chong's fortress cannot match such grace.

sentences.zh: 既未奉朝旨，無由親馳道路，謹遣大息景徽，束骸歸闕，伏聽刑斧。」

translations.literal: Not yet having received court instruction, I had no way to hurry along the road in person; I respectfully send my eldest son Jinghui, binding my bones to return to court, to prostrate and await the executioner's axe."
translations.idiomatic: Not having yet received court orders, I cannot come in person; I respectfully send my eldest son Jinghui, offering my body to the court to lie beneath the axe."

sentences.zh: 既而白曜送道固赴都，有司案劾，奏聞，詔恕其死。

translations.literal: Before long Baiyao escorted Daogu to the capital; the relevant offices investigated and reported, and an edict pardoned his death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Baiyao sent Daogu to the capital; the ministries investigated and reported up, and an edict spared his life.

sentences.zh: 乃徙青齊士望共道固守城者數百家於桑乾，立平齊郡於平城西北北新城。

translations.literal: Then several hundred families of Qing and Qi scholar-gentry who had held the city with Daogu were moved to Sanggan; Pingqi commandery was established northwest of Beixin cheng in Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred leading families of Qing and Qi who had held the city with him were moved to Sanggan, and Pingqi commandery was set up northwest of Beixin cheng near Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 以道固為太守，賜爵臨淄子，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Daogu was made its prefect, granted the title Marquis of Linzi, and given the additional rank General Who Calms the North.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was made prefect, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linzi, and given the added title general who calms the north.

sentences.zh: 尋徙治京城西南二百餘里舊陰館之西。

translations.literal: Soon the seat was moved to the west of old Yinguan, more than two hundred li southwest of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the commandery seat was shifted west of old Yinguan, over two hundred li southwest of the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，頻歲不登，郡內飢弊，道固雖在任積年，撫慰未能周盡，是以多有怨叛。

translations.literal: At that time harvests failed year after year; within the commandery there was famine and distress. Though Daogu held office for many years, his comforting care could not reach everywhere, and therefore there were many resentments and rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: Famine followed famine; the commandery starved. Though Daogu held office for years, he could not ease every district, and rebellions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 延興中卒，年五十。

translations.literal: He died in Yanxing at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanxing at fifty.

sentences.zh: 初，道固之在客邸，與薛安都畢眾敬隣館，時以朝集相見，本既同由武達，頗結僚舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Daogu was lodged as a guest, he shared neighboring quarters with Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing; at morning assemblies they met. Originally both had risen through military paths and had formed colleague ties.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogu was a guest at court he lodged beside Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing; they met at morning levees. All three had risen through military service and were old colleagues.

sentences.zh: 時安都志已衰朽，於道固情乃疏略，而眾敬每盡殷勤。

translations.literal: By then Andu's ambition was already decayed; toward Daogu his feeling grew sparse, while Zhongjing every time showed full earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: By then Andu's spirit was failing and his warmth toward Daogu had cooled, while Zhongjing was unfailingly attentive.

sentences.zh: 道固謂劉休賓、房法壽曰：「古人云『非我族類，其心必異』，信不虛也。

translations.literal: Daogu said to Liu Xiubin and Fang Fashou: "The ancients said, 'Those not of our kind — their hearts surely differ' — it is not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu told Liu Xiubin and Fang Fashou: "The ancients said, 'Those not of our kind will surely differ in heart' — and it is true.

sentences.zh: 安都視人殊自蕭索，畢捺固依依也。」

translations.literal: Andu views people quite detached; Bi Naya is still clinging."
translations.idiomatic: Andu looks on people coldly; Bi Naya still clings close."

sentences.zh: 子景徽，字文叡，襲父爵臨淄子，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: His son Jinghui, styled Wenrui, inherited his father's title Marquis of Linzi and was given the additional rank General Who Calms the North.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinghui, styled Wenrui, succeeded to the marquisate of Linzi and was given the added title general who calms the north.

sentences.zh: 出為青州廣陵王羽征東府司馬、大鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He went out as eastern-campaign staff vice marshal to Guangling Prince Yu of Qingzhou and as vice minister of the grand court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as eastern-campaign vice marshal on Guangling Prince Yu's staff in Qingzhou and as vice minister of the grand court.

sentences.zh: 出除龍驤將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as dragon-charging general and inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made dragon-charging general and inspector of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received his former rank, southern Qingzhou inspector, with the posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously he kept his former rank and was named southern Qingzhou inspector, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子休纂襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xiuzuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiuzuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 景徽弟景業，字文季。

translations.literal: Jinghui's younger brother Jingye, styled Wenji.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghui's younger brother Jingye, styled Wenji — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 別有功，太和中，賜爵昌國子，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: He had separate merit; in the Taihe era he was granted the title Marquis of Changguo and the added rank General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He earned separate merit; in the Taihe era he was made Marquis of Changguo and general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子休緒襲爵，員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Xiuxu inherited the title and was an outer-office gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiuxu succeeded and served as outer-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 景業弟景淵，亦有別功，賜爵武城男。

translations.literal: Jingye's younger brother Jingyuan also had separate merit and was granted the title Baron of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye's younger brother Jingyuan also won separate merit and was made Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 鷹揚將軍、平齊太守。

translations.literal: He was eagle-brandishing general and prefect of Pingqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was eagle-brandishing general and prefect of Pingqi — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 道固兄目連子僧祐。

translations.literal: Daogu's brother Mulian's son Sengyou.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou was son of Daogu's brother Mulian.

sentences.zh: 白曜之圍歷城也，僧祐母明氏、弟僧淵並在城內。

translations.literal: When Baiyao besieged Licheng, Sengyou's mother, of the Ming clan, and his younger brother Sengyuan were all in the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiyao besieged Licheng, Sengyou's mother, Lady Ming, and his brother Sengyuan were inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 劉彧授僧祐輔國將軍，領眾數千，與青齊人家口在歷城、梁鄒者明同慶、明菩薩等為將佐，從淮海揚聲救援。

translations.literal: Liu Yu appointed Sengyou auxiliary-state general, leading several thousand troops; with Qing and Qi families in Licheng and Liangzou — Ming Tongqing, Ming Pusa, and others as staff officers — he raised a rescue cry from Huaihai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu made Sengyou auxiliary-state general at the head of several thousand men; with Qing and Qi kin still in Licheng and Liangzou — Ming Tongqing, Ming Pusa, and others on his staff — he marched from Huaihai shouting rescue.

sentences.zh: 將至不其，聞道固已敗，母弟入國，徘徊不進。

translations.literal: When he was about to reach Buqi, he heard Daogu had already been defeated and that his mother and brother had entered the state; he hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Near Buqi he learned that Daogu had fallen and that his mother and brother were already in Wei; he halted and would not go on.

sentences.zh: 白曜圍東陽時，表請景徽往喻僧祐，乃歸降。

translations.literal: When Baiyao besieged Dongyang, he memorialized requesting Jinghui go to persuade Sengyou; Sengyou then returned and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiyao besieged Dongyang, he asked that Jinghui be sent to win over Sengyou; Sengyou then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 白曜送之，在客數載，賜爵層城侯。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent him in; as a guest for several years he was granted the title Marquis of Tiered City.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent him to court; after several years as a guest he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tiered City.

sentences.zh: 與房法壽、畢薩諸人皆不穆。

translations.literal: He was on bad terms with Fang Fashou, Bi Sa, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was at odds with Fang Fashou, Bi Sa, and the rest.

sentences.zh: [15]法壽等訟其歸國無誠，拘之歲餘，因赦乃釋。

translations.literal: [15] Fashou and others sued that his return to the state lacked sincerity; he was detained for more than a year and released only by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: [15] Fashou and others charged that his surrender was insincere; he was held more than a year and freed only by a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後坐與沙門法秀謀反，伏法。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted for plotting rebellion with the monk Faxiu and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was convicted of plotting rebellion with the monk Faxiu and was executed.

sentences.zh: 子道寧，給事中。

translations.literal: His son Daoning was a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoning served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 僧淵入國，坐兄弟徙於薄骨律鎮，太和初得還。

translations.literal: Sengyuan entered Wei territory; because of his brother he was exiled to Boguli Garrison; at the beginning of the Taihe era he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan came into Wei lands; on account of his brother he was exiled to Boguli Garrison and at the opening of the Taihe era was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞其有文學，又問佛經，善談論，敕以白衣賜褠幘，入聽于永樂經武殿。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard he had learning and questioned him on Buddhist sutras; skilled in discourse, he ordered that though in lay dress he be granted a black headcloth and admitted to listen at the Yongle Jingwu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of his scholarship, questioned him on Buddhist sutras, and found him skilled in debate; he ordered that though still in lay dress Sengyuan receive a black cap and attend lectures in the Yongle Jingwu Hall.

sentences.zh: 後以僧淵為尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Later Sengyuan was appointed Gentleman of the Protocol Section in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made gentleman of the protocol section in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷洛之後，為青州中正。

translations.literal: After the move of the capital to Luoyang he was chief rectifier of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang he served as chief rectifier of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋出為征東大將軍、廣陵王羽諮議參軍，加顯武將軍，討海賊於黃郭，[16]大破之。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as staff counselor to the general who campaigns east, Grand General and Prince of Guangling Yu, with the additional title General of Illustrious Martiality; he attacked sea bandits at Huangguo [16] and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left court as staff counselor to the eastern campaign grand general, Prince of Guangling Yu, with the added title general of illustrious martiality; he attacked sea bandits at Huangguo [16] and routed them.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞乃遣其族兄惠景遺僧淵書，說以入國之屈，規令改圖。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan thereupon sent his clansman elder brother Huijing to leave a letter for Sengyuan, explaining the hardship of entering Wei and urging him to change course.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan then sent his elder clansman Huijing with a letter to Sengyuan, pleading the wrong of his coming into Wei and urging him to change his course.

sentences.zh: 僧淵復書曰：

translations.literal: Sengyuan replied in writing:
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan wrote back:

sentences.zh: 主上之為人也，無幽不照，無細不存，仁則無遠不及，博則無典不究，殫三墳之微，盡九丘之極。

translations.literal: The sovereign's conduct as a man — nothing hidden escapes his light, nothing small escapes his care; in benevolence none so far he does not reach; in breadth no classic he does not exhaust; he exhausts the subtlety of the Three Storehouses and the utmost of the Nine Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord's nature as a man leaves no dark place unlit and no small thing uncared for; in kindness there is no distance he cannot reach, in learning no canon he has not mastered — he has drained the subtlety of the Three Storehouses and the limits of the Nine Mounds.

sentences.zh: 至於文章錯綜，煥然蔚炳，猶夫子之牆矣。

translations.literal: As for his literary compositions woven in complexity, brilliantly lustrous — they are like the Master's wall.
translations.idiomatic: His woven prose blazes with color like the wall of the Master himself.

sentences.zh: 遂乃開獨悟之明，尋先王之迹，安遷靈荒，兆變帝基，惟新中壤，宅臨伊域。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the clarity of solitary awakening, traced the footprints of former kings, settled the desolate borderlands, presaged change in the imperial foundation, renewed the central lands, and dwelt facing the Yi domain.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a solitary clarity of mind, traced the tracks of former kings, settled the wild marches, foretold change in the imperial foundation, renewed the central lands, and made his seat on the Yi banks.

sentences.zh: 三光起重輝之照，庶物蒙再化之始。

translations.literal: The three luminaries regained the illumination of renewed brilliance; the myriad things received the beginning of a second transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The three lights shone again with renewed splendor; the myriad things received a second birth.

sentences.zh: 分氏定族，料甲乙之科；

translations.literal: He sorted clans and fixed descent, assessing grades of first and second class;
translations.idiomatic: He sorted clans and fixed descent, grading households into first and second ranks;

sentences.zh: 班官命爵，清九流之貫。

translations.literal: He arrayed offices and granted noble ranks, clarifying the thread of the nine currents.
translations.idiomatic: he arrayed offices and granted noble ranks, clearing the thread of the nine currents.

sentences.zh: 禮俗之敍，粲然復興，河洛之間，重隆周道。

translations.literal: The ordering of ritual and custom blazed forth in revival; between the Yellow and Luo the Zhou Way was raised high again.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and custom blazed back to life; between the Yellow and Luo the Zhou Way rose again.

sentences.zh: 巷歌邑頌，朝熙門穆，濟濟之盛，非可備陳矣。

translations.literal: Lane songs and district hymns, courts radiant and gates serene — such flourishing abundance cannot be fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Lane songs and district hymns, radiant courts and tranquil gates — such flourishing cannot be told in full.

sentences.zh: 加以累葉重光，地兼四岳，士馬強富，人神欣仰，道德仁義，民不能名。

translations.literal: Added to this, generation upon generation of doubled glory, a domain embracing the four sacred peaks, soldiers and horses strong and rich, men and spirits rejoicing in reverence — virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness the people cannot name.
translations.idiomatic: Add generation upon generation of doubled glory, a domain holding the four sacred peaks, strong hosts and rich stores, men and spirits rejoicing — virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 且大人出，本無所在，況從上聖至天子天孫者乎。

translations.literal: Moreover when a great man appears, he has no fixed place of origin — how much more when one descends from the highest sage to Heaven's grandson?
translations.idiomatic: When a great man appears he has no fixed birthplace — how much more one who descends from the highest sage to Heaven's grandson?

sentences.zh: [17]聖上諸弟，風度相類，咸陽王已下，莫不英越，枝葉扶疎，遍在天下，所稱稍竭，[18]殊為未然。

translations.literal: [17] The sovereign's younger brothers share a matching bearing; from the Prince of Xianyang down, none without outstanding excellence; branches and leaves luxuriant, spread through the realm; that their renown is somewhat spent [18] is wholly premature.
translations.idiomatic: [17] The sovereign's younger brothers share one bearing; from the Prince of Xianyang down, none without surpassing talent; branches and leaves spread through the realm — that their fame is already fading [18] is far too soon.

sentences.zh: 文士競謀於廟堂，武夫效勇於疆埸，[19]若論事勢，此為實矣。

translations.literal: Literati vie in counsel at the court; warriors display courage on the frontier — [19] if one reckons the true situation of affairs, this is the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars contend in counsel at court, soldiers show courage on the marches — [19] judge the true situation and this is fact.

sentences.zh: 計彼主篡殺之迹，人鬼同知，疑親猜貴，早暴遐邇。

translations.literal: Consider the traces of that lord's usurpation and murder — known alike to men and spirits; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble long ago exposed far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh that lord's usurpation and murder — known to men and spirits alike; suspicion of kin and mistrust of the noble were long ago plain far and near.

sentences.zh: 兄投心逆節，千載何名！

translations.literal: Elder brother, to cast your heart into rebellion — what name for a thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother, to set your heart on rebellion — what name will stand for a thousand years?

sentences.zh: 物患無施，器非時用，生不振世，沒無令聲，先師以為鄙，君子以為耻。

translations.literal: When things have no scope for use and vessels are unfit for the time, one who lives without stirring the age and dies without a fair reputation — the former masters held this base, gentlemen held it shameful.
translations.idiomatic: When things have no place to be used and vessels are unfit for the age, to live without stirring the world and die without a fair name — the ancients called that base, gentlemen called it shame.

sentences.zh: 此則事困伎殫，自勉無益，故其宜矣。

translations.literal: Here events are straitened and skills exhausted; self-exhortation brings no gain — hence the fit course.
translations.idiomatic: Here affairs are tight and arts spent; urging oneself on brings no gain — hence the proper course.

sentences.zh: 以兄之才，夙超鄉土，如弟之徒，誰不瞻仰，每尋昔念，未敢忘懷。

translations.literal: With elder brother's talent, from old surpassing your homeland — who among men like me does not look up to you? Whenever I recall former thoughts, I dare not forget.
translations.idiomatic: With your talent, elder brother, you have long outshone our homeland — who like me does not look up to you? I never dare forget our old bond.

sentences.zh: 雖復途遙二千，心想若對，敬遵軌範，以資一生。

translations.literal: Though the road spans two thousand li, in thought we meet face to face; reverently I follow the norm and draw on it for a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Though two thousand li lie between us, in thought we meet as face to face; reverently I follow your example for my whole life.

sentences.zh: 今名可揚矣而不能顯親，事可變矣而不能離辱，故世之所未解也。

translations.literal: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot glorify kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot leave disgrace — hence what the age has not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Now fame could be raised yet you cannot honor your kin; affairs could be changed yet you cannot shake off disgrace — that is what the age cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 且君子在家也不過孝於其親，入朝也不過忠於其君。

translations.literal: And the gentleman at home does no more than show filial piety to his kin; in court does no more than show loyalty to his lord.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman at home is filial to his kin; in court he is loyal to his lord — no more.

sentences.zh: 主上之於兄，恩則不可酬，義則不可背。

translations.literal: The sovereign's treatment of elder brother — in grace it cannot be repaid, in righteousness it cannot be betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's treatment of you, elder brother — grace that cannot be repaid, righteousness that cannot be betrayed.

sentences.zh: 身可殺也，故非其酬；

translations.literal: The person may be killed — hence this is not the repayment;
translations.idiomatic: One's person may be given up — that is not repayment;

sentences.zh: 功不逮也，故非其報。

translations.literal: Merit does not reach so far — hence this is not the return.
translations.idiomatic: merit does not stretch so far — that is not return.

sentences.zh: 今可以效矣而又弗為，非孝也。

translations.literal: Now you could effect loyalty yet again do not — this is unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Now you could act loyally and again you will not — that is unfilial.

sentences.zh: 即實而言，兄之不變，得為忠乎？

translations.literal: Judged by fact, elder brother's not changing — can this count as loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Judged by fact, elder brother, can your refusal to change count as loyalty?

sentences.zh: 至於講武爭強，不敵者久矣；

translations.literal: As for training in arms and contending for supremacy, the unmatched have long been so;
translations.idiomatic: As for drilling in arms and contending for mastery, you have long been unmatched;

sentences.zh: 論安與危，不同者驗矣；

translations.literal: Discussing security and danger, those not alike have been proved;
translations.idiomatic: weigh safety against peril and the unlike cases have been proved;

sentences.zh: 羣情背去，獨留者謬矣。

translations.literal: Mass sentiment turns away in desertion; to remain alone is error.
translations.idiomatic: the crowd's heart has turned away — to stand alone is error.

sentences.zh: [20]願深察之。

translations.literal: [20] I beg deep scrutiny of this.
translations.idiomatic: [20] I beg you to weigh this deeply.

sentences.zh: 王晏道絕外交，器非雄朗，專華保望，便就屠割。

translations.literal: Wang Yan utterly cut off external ties; his capacity was not heroic and bright; clinging to splendor and guarding hope, he was at once sent to slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan cut off every outside tie; his talent was not bold and bright; clinging to glory and nursing hope, he was at once put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 方之於兄，其全百倍。

translations.literal: Compared with elder brother, you are whole a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with you, elder brother, he was not one part in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 且淮蕃海捍，本出北豪，壽春之任，兄何由免？

translations.literal: Moreover the Huai lands and the coastal marches originally produced northern champions — could elder brother escape the charge at Shouchun?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Huai frontier and the coastal garrisons bred northern champions — could you, elder brother, escape the Shouchun command?

sentences.zh: 以是而言，猜嫌已決。

translations.literal: On this ground, suspicion and mistrust are already settled.
translations.idiomatic: On that ground suspicion is already fixed.

sentences.zh: 又宗門未幾，南北莫寄，先構之重，非兄何託，受社之榮，鄙心之相望矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the ancestral house is not many generations old; north and south have no other lodging — to whom but elder brother can the weight of the prior structure be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — this humble heart has longed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the house is still young; north and south have nowhere else to lodge — to whom but you, elder brother, can the weight of the founding be entrusted? The glory of receiving a fief — my humble heart has long looked for it.

sentences.zh: 今執志不寤，忠孝兩忘，王晏之辜，安能自保，見機而作，其在茲乎。

translations.literal: Now clinging to resolve without waking, both filial piety and loyalty forgotten — Wang Yan's crime, how can he protect himself? To act when the moment appears — is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: Now you cling to your resolve without waking, forgetting both filial piety and loyalty — Wang Yan's guilt, how could he save himself? To act when the moment shows itself — is it not now?

sentences.zh: 國家西至長安，東盡即墨，營造器甲，必盡堅精，晝夜不息者，於茲數載。

translations.literal: The state from Chang'an in the west to Jimo in the east — forging armor and weapons — all to utmost solidity and keenness; day and night without cease for these several years.
translations.idiomatic: The state from Chang'an in the west to Jimo in the east has forged armor and weapons to utmost solidity and keen edge, day and night without cease these several years.

sentences.zh: 今秋中月，雲羅必舉，賈不及時，雖貴不用，若不早圖，況枉連城矣。

translations.literal: In the middle month of autumn this year the cloud net will surely rise; goods that miss the season, though costly, are not used — if you do not plan early, what of wronging a linked city?
translations.idiomatic: This mid-autumn the cloud-net will surely be cast; goods that miss the season, though precious, are not used — if you do not plan early, how will you answer for a city worth a thousand?

sentences.zh: [21]枚乘有言，欲出不出，間不容髮，精哉斯談。

translations.literal: [21] Mei Cheng said: wanting to go out yet not going out, no space between for a hair — how refined that saying!
translations.idiomatic: [21] Mei Cheng said: wanting to go out yet not going out — no room for a hair between — how fine that saying!

sentences.zh: 弟中於北京，身罹事譴，大造之及，有獲為幸。

translations.literal: Your younger brother struck at Beijing, personally suffered penal summons; that the Great Making reached me was fortune obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother was struck down at the northern capital and personally bore penal summons; that the great grace reached me was luck won.

sentences.zh: 比蒙清舉，超進非一，[22]犬馬之心，誠有在矣。

translations.literal: Recently I have been repeatedly promoted by clear selection beyond counting — [22] the heart of dog and horse truly has its place.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have been raised again and again by clear selection, more than once — [22] the heart of dog and horse truly has its master.

sentences.zh: 雖復彼此為異，猶昔情不移也，況於今日哉。

translations.literal: Though now we stand on opposite sides, the old feeling is unchanged — how much more today?
translations.idiomatic: Though we now stand on opposite sides, the old feeling is unchanged — how much more so today?

sentences.zh: 如兄之誨，如弟之規，改張易調，易於反掌，萬一乖情，此將運也。

translations.literal: Like elder brother's teaching, like younger brother's counsel — to change the tuning and reset the strings is easier than turning the palm; if feeling should once go awry, that will be fate.
translations.idiomatic: As elder brother teaches, as younger brother urges — to change the tuning is easier than turning the palm; if feeling should once go wrong, that will be fate.

sentences.zh: 出除龍驤將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out and was dismissed as Dragon-Charging General and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as dragon-charging general and inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，坐擅出師無據，檢覈幽禁，後乃獲免。

translations.literal: After long time, convicted of campaigning out without warrant; investigated and confined; later he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was convicted of campaigning out without warrant, investigated and imprisoned; later he was released.

sentences.zh: 僧淵元妻房氏生二子伯驎、伯驥。

translations.literal: Sengyuan's first wife, Lady Fang, bore two sons, Bolin and Boji.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan's first wife, the Fang clan, bore two sons, Bolin and Boji.

sentences.zh: 後薄房氏，更納平原杜氏。

translations.literal: Later he slighted the Fang clan and took the Du clan of Pingyuan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later he slighted the Fang and married the Du of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 僧淵之徙也，與杜俱去，生四子，伯鳳、祖龍、祖螭、祖虬。

translations.literal: When Sengyuan was exiled he went with Du and bore four sons: Bofeng, Zulong, Zuchi, and Zuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengyuan was exiled he went with Du and she bore four sons — Bofeng, Zulong, Zuchi, and Zuqiu.

sentences.zh: 得還之後，棄絕房氏，遂與杜氏及四子家于青州。

translations.literal: After his return he abandoned Lady Fang and settled in Qingzhou with the Du clan and the four sons.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned he cast off the Fang and made his home in Qingzhou with Du and the four sons.

sentences.zh: 伯驥與母房氏居于冀州，雖往來父間，而心存母氏，孝慈之道，頓阻一門。

translations.literal: Boji lived with his mother Lady Fang in Jizhou; though he went back and forth to his father, his heart remained with his mother — filial and kindly duty was suddenly blocked within one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Boji lived with his mother the Fang in Jizhou; though he visited his father, his heart stayed with his mother — filial kindness was cut off within one household.

sentences.zh: 僧淵卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: Sengyuan died at over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan died aged over seventy.

sentences.zh: 伯驎雖往奔赴，不敢入家，哭沙門寺。

translations.literal: Bolin though he hurried to the funeral did not dare enter the house and wept at a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: Bolin hurried to the funeral but dared not enter the house and wept at a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 伯驎，自奉朝請，稍遷步兵校尉、樂陵太守，加中堅將軍。

translations.literal: Bolin, from court attendant, was gradually promoted to infantry commandant and governor of Leling, with the additional title general of the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: Bolin rose from court attendant to infantry commandant and governor of Leling, with the added title general of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 後兼冀州長史。

translations.literal: Later he also served as chief clerk of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also served as chief clerk of Jizhou — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 大乘賊起，伯驎率州軍討之於煮棗城，為賊所殺，贈龍驤將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Dacheng rebels rose, Bolin led the provincial army against them at Zhushao walled town and was killed by the rebels; he was posthumously made dragon-charging general and governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dacheng rebels rose, Bolin led the provincial army against them at Zhushao and was killed; he was posthumously made dragon-charging general and governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 伯驥，為京兆王愉法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Boji was a legal affairs staff officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Boji was legal-affairs staff officer to the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉反，伯驥不從，見害，詔贈東海太守。

translations.literal: When Yu rebelled, Boji would not follow and was killed; an edict posthumously made him governor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rebelled, Boji refused to follow and was killed; an edict posthumously made him governor of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 伯鳳，少便弓馬，壯勇有膂力。

translations.literal: Bofeng from youth was skilled in bow and horse; in maturity brave and strong in the arm.
translations.idiomatic: Bofeng from youth was skilled with bow and horse; grown, he was bold and powerful.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請、員外郎，稍遷鎮遠將軍、前將軍，數為將帥。

translations.literal: From court attendant and outer-office gentleman he was gradually promoted to general who pacifies the distance and forward general, and several times served as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: From court attendant and outer-office gentleman he rose step by step to general who pacifies the distance and forward general and several times held field command.

sentences.zh: 永安末，與都督源子恭守丹谷，戰歿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yong'an era, with the area commander Yuan Zigong he held Dan Valley and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yong'an era he held Dan Valley with area commander Yuan Zigong and died in battle.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 祖龍，司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Zulong was a staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zulong was a staff officer in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 性剛躁，父亡後，與兄伯驎訟競嫡庶，並以刀劍自衞，若怨讎焉。

translations.literal: By nature harsh and impetuous, after his father's death he contended with his elder brother Bolin over legitimacy of birth, each guarding himself with sword and blade as if against a foe.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and impetuous by nature, after his father's death he sued his elder brother Bolin over legitimacy of birth, each keeping sword and blade as against an enemy.

sentences.zh: 祖螭，小字社客，粗武有氣力。

translations.literal: Zuchi, childhood name Sheke, was rough in martial bearing and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchi, childhood name Sheke, was rough and martial and strong in the arm.

sentences.zh: 刺史元羅板為兼統軍，率眾討海賊。

translations.literal: Inspector Yuan Luo installed him as acting commander-in-chief and led troops to attack sea bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yuan Luo installed him as acting commander-in-chief and led troops against sea bandits.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，與張僧皓俱反，圍青州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Putai era he rebelled together with Zhang Senghao and besieged Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Putai era he rebelled with Zhang Senghao and besieged Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尒朱仲遠遣將討平之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent a general to suppress them; their heads were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent a general to crush them; their heads were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 祖虬，少而好學，下帷誦書，不驅競當世。

translations.literal: Zuqiu from youth loved learning; he drew the curtain and recited books, not striving with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zuqiu from youth loved learning; he studied behind closed curtains and did not vie with the world.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才不就。

translations.literal: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as cultivated talent, he would not take office.

sentences.zh: 僧淵從弟和，平昌太守。

translations.literal: Sengyuan's younger cousin He was governor of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan's younger cousin He was governor of Pingchang — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 家巨富，而性吝嗇，埋錢數百斛。

translations.literal: The household was immensely rich yet by nature stingy; he buried cash in hundreds of hu.
translations.idiomatic: The house was immensely rich yet he was stingy by nature and buried cash in hundreds of hu.

sentences.zh: 其母李春思堇，惜錢不買。

translations.literal: His mother Chunsi craved purslane; he begrudged the cash and would not buy it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Chunsi longed for purslane; he begrudged the money and would not buy it.

sentences.zh: 子軌，字啟則，盜錢百萬，背和亡走。

translations.literal: His son Gui, styled Qize, stole a million in cash and fled, turning his back on He.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui, styled Qize, stole a million in cash and fled, abandoning He.

sentences.zh: 後為儀同開府鎧曹參軍，坐貪汙，死於晉陽。

translations.literal: Later he was a staff officer in the office of armor for the ceremonial peer with open office; convicted of corruption, he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was armor-office staff officer to a ceremonial peer with open office; convicted of corruption, he died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 玄伯同郡董謐。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's fellow commandery man Dong Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Mi came from Xuanbo's commandery.

sentences.zh: 謐父京，與同郡崔康時、廣陽霍原等，俱以碩學播名遼海。

translations.literal: Mi's father Jing, together with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery, Huo Yuan of Guangyang, and others, all spread their great learning's fame through Liaohai.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery, Huo Yuan of Guangyang, and others, all spread the fame of great learning through Liaohai.

sentences.zh: 謐好學，傳父業。

translations.literal: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's profession.
translations.idiomatic: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.

sentences.zh: 中山平，入朝，拜儀曹郎，撰朝覲饗宴郊廟社稷之儀。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court and was appointed Gentleman of the Protocol Section, drafting the rites for court audience, feasting, suburban sacrifice, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court as gentleman of the protocol section and drafted the rites for court audience, banquets, suburban sacrifice, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 鄧淵，字彥海，安定人也。

translations.literal: Deng Yuan, styled Yanhai, was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuan, styled Yanhai, came from Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖羌，苻堅車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang was chariot general under Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang was chariot general under Fu Jian — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 父翼，河間相。

translations.literal: His father Yi was governor of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was governor of Hejian — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂之圍鄴，以翼為後將軍、冀州刺史、真定侯。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, he made Yi rear general, inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui besieged Ye he made Yi rear general, inspector of Jizhou, and Marquis of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 翼泣對使者曰：「先君忠于秦室，翼豈可先叛乎！

translations.literal: Yi wept and said to the envoy: "My late father was loyal to the house of Qin — how could Yi be first to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Yi wept and told the envoy: "My late father was loyal to Qin — how could Yi be the first to rebel?

sentences.zh: 忠臣不事二主，自古通義，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: A loyal minister does not serve two lords — from antiquity the constant principle; I dare not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister does not serve two lords — that is the constant rule since antiquity; I dare not accept the order.

sentences.zh: 」垂遣使喻之曰：「吾與車騎結異姓兄弟，卿亦猶吾之子弟，安得辭乎？

translations.literal: " Chui sent an envoy to persuade him: "I and the chariot general became sworn brothers of different surnames; you too are like my own son or younger brother — how can you decline?
translations.idiomatic: " Chui sent an envoy to persuade him: "Your grandfather the chariot general and I became sworn brothers of different surnames; you are like my own son or younger brother — how can you refuse?

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「冀州宜任親賢，翼請他役效命。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Jizhou should be entrusted to kin and the worthy; Yi asks for another duty to offer his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said: "Jizhou should go to kin and the worthy; let Yi serve in another post and offer his life.

sentences.zh: 」垂乃用為建武將軍、河間太守、尚書左丞，皆有聲稱。

translations.literal: " Chui thereupon employed him as General of Establishing Martiality, governor of Hejian, and Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat — in each post he won reputation.
translations.idiomatic: " Chui then used him as general of establishing martiality, governor of Hejian, and left deputy director of the secretariat — in each post he won praise.

sentences.zh: 卒於趙郡內史。

translations.literal: He died as inner governor of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died as inner governor of Zhao commandery — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 淵性貞素，言行可復，博覽經書，長於易筮。

translations.literal: Yuan by nature was upright and plain; his words and conduct could be relied on; he ranged broadly through the classics; he excelled in the Changes and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was upright and plain by nature, his words and conduct trustworthy; he ranged widely through the classics and excelled in the Changes and divination.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中原，擢為著作郎。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified the central plains he was promoted to Gentleman of the Composition Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified the central plains he was raised to gentleman of the composition office.

sentences.zh: 出為蒲丘令，誅剪姦猾，盜賊肅清。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Puqiu and cut down the crafty and violent; bandits were cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as magistrate of Puqiu, cut down the crafty and violent, and cleared away bandits.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 淵明解制度，多識舊事，與尚書崔玄伯參定朝儀、律令、音樂，及軍國文記詔策，多淵所為。

translations.literal: Yuan clearly understood institutions, knew many old precedents, and with Masters of Writing Cui Xuanbo jointly fixed court ritual, laws and orders, music, and military and state records, edicts and policies — most of it was Yuan's work.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had a clear grasp of institutions and old precedent; with Cui Xuanbo of the Masters of Writing he shaped court ritual, statutes, music, and the military and state archives, edicts and policies — most of it was Yuan's hand.

sentences.zh: 從征平陽，以功賜爵漢昌子，改下博子，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Pingyang he was rewarded with the enfeoffment Marquis of Hankang; it was changed to Marquis of Xiabo and he was made General of the Central Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: On the Pingyang campaign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hankang, then made Marquis of Xiabo and general of the central rampart.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔淵撰國記，淵造十餘卷，惟次年月起居行事而已，未有體例。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Yuan to compile the national record; Yuan produced more than ten scrolls, only year-by-year daily affairs and conduct, with no formal pattern yet.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor charged Yuan to compile the national record; he drafted more than ten scrolls of year-by-year court affairs only, without a settled form.

sentences.zh: 淵謹於朝事，未嘗忤旨。

translations.literal: Yuan was scrupulous in court business and never went against the throne's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was exacting in court affairs and never crossed the sovereign's will.

sentences.zh: 其從父弟暉為尚書郎，兇俠好奇，與定陵侯和跋厚善。

translations.literal: His younger cousin by the father's line, Hui, was a Masters of Writing gentleman — fierce and fond of adventure, thick friends with Marquis of Dingling He Ba.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin's son Hui was a gentleman in the Masters of Writing — violent, restless, and close to Marquis of Dingling He Ba.

sentences.zh: 跋有罪誅，其子弟奔長安，或告暉將送出之。

translations.literal: When Ba was executed for crime, his sons and younger brothers fled to Chang'an; someone reported that Hui would send them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba was put to death for his crimes, his kin fled to Chang'an; someone said Hui meant to smuggle them out.

sentences.zh: 由是太祖疑淵知情，遂賜淵死，既而恨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Founding Emperor suspected Yuan knew of it and ordered Yuan to die; afterward he regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor then suspected Yuan had known and had Yuan put to death — and afterward regretted it.

sentences.zh: 時人咸愍惜焉。

translations.literal: Men of the time all pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it mourned him.

sentences.zh: 子潁，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ying inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 為太學生，稍遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was a student of the Imperial Academy and was gradually promoted to Attendant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Imperial Academy and rose step by step to secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔太常崔浩集諸文學，撰述國書，潁與浩弟覽等俱參著作事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered Grand Minister of Ceremonials Cui Hao to gather literary men to compile the dynastic history; Ying, with Hao's younger brother Lan and others, all took part in the writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered Grand Minister of Ceremonials Cui Hao to gather scholars to compile the dynastic history; Ying joined Hao's brother Lan and others on the work.

sentences.zh: 駕幸漠南，高車莫弗庫若干率騎數萬餘，驅鹿百餘萬，詣行在所。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the desert south, the Gaoche chieftain Mofu Kugan led tens of thousands of horsemen driving more than a million deer to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the court visited the southern desert, the Gaoche chief Mofu Kugan brought tens of thousands of riders driving more than a million deer to the encampment.

sentences.zh: 詔潁為文，銘于漠南，以紀功德。

translations.literal: An edict made Ying compose a text and inscribe it in the desert south to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was ordered to write and set up an inscription in the southern desert to commemorate the feat.

sentences.zh: 兼散騎常侍，使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: He was also made Acting Regular Attendant and sent on mission to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made acting regular attendant and sent as envoy to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to marquis and made Dragon-Charging General.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis and made dragon-charging general.

sentences.zh: 延和三年，從征胡賊白龍。

translations.literal: In Yanhe year 3 he followed the campaign against the Hu bandit Bai Long.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanhe year 3 he joined the campaign against the Hu rebel Bai Long.

sentences.zh: 還，卒於路。

translations.literal: On the return he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the march home.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子怡，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 官至荊州刺史、假寧南將軍。

translations.literal: He reached the posts Inspector of Jingzhou and Acting Pacifying-South General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jingzhou inspector and acting pacifying-south general.

sentences.zh: 賜爵南陽公。

translations.literal: He was granted the enfeoffment Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 和平中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Heping era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Heping era — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 長子良奴，襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Liangnu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Liangnu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 良奴弟侍高祖，賜名述。

translations.literal: Liangnu's younger brother attended Emperor Gaozu and was granted the name Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liangnu's younger brother attended Emperor Gaozu and was given the name Shu.

sentences.zh: 歷吏職，以貞謹見稱。

translations.literal: He passed through civil offices and was praised for integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: He served in civil posts and was praised for upright care.

sentences.zh: 遷中大夫，守廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of the Palace and Acting Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of the palace and acting vice director of the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 出為建忠將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Loyalty and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as general who establishes loyalty and Qi inspector.

sentences.zh: 初改置百官，始重公府元佐。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were first reorganized, the chief aides of the great offices were newly weighted.
translations.idiomatic: At the first reshaping of the hundred offices, chief aides to the great ministries were given new weight.

sentences.zh: 時太傅元丕出為并州刺史，以述為太傅長史，帶太原太守。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Tutor Yuan Pi went out as Inspector of Bing Province; Shu was made Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor, concurrently Taiyuan Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Tutor Yuan Pi went out as Bing inspector, Shu was made his chief clerk and concurrently Taiyuan administrator.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為司空長史，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as chief clerk to the minister of works and died in his post.

sentences.zh: 詔賜錢十萬、布五十匹，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: An edict granted one hundred thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted one hundred thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; his posthumous name was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長子纂，奉朝請，累遷中散大夫。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuan was a court attendant and rose through posts to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zuan was a court attendant and rose to grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 纂弟獻，奉朝請、司空西閤祭酒、員外常侍、河陰令。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Xian was court attendant, Sacrificer in the Western Pavilion of the Minister of Works, Outer Regular Attendant, and Magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Xian was court attendant, sacrifier in the minister of works' western pavilion, outer regular attendant, and Heyin magistrate.

sentences.zh: 尋遷鎮遠將軍、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who pacifies the distance and remonstrance and policy grand master.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，除冠軍將軍、潁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he was made Champion General and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Suzong's reign he was made champion general and Ying inspector.

sentences.zh: 建義初，聞尒朱榮入洛，朝士見害，遂奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Jianyi era, hearing that Erzhu Rong had entered Luoyang and court gentlemen were being killed, he fled to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyi, when he heard Erzhu Rong had entered Luoyang and courtiers were being killed, he fled to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 怡弟宗慶，以中書學生，入為中散。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Zongqing, from a student of the Secretariat, entered service as Central Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Zongqing, starting as a secretariat student, entered service as central court attendant.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書，加散騎常侍，賜爵定安侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Masters of Writing, with Acting Regular Attendant added, and granted the enfeoffment Marquis of Ding'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to the Masters of Writing, was given acting regular attendant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 轉典南部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to director of the southern bureau.

sentences.zh: 宗慶在南部積年，多所敷奏，州鎮憚之，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Zongqing spent many years in the Southern Bureau and submitted many memorials; provinces and garrisons feared him, and he was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing spent years in the southern bureau and filed many memorials; provinces and garrisons feared him and called him fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 進爵南陽公，除安南將軍、涇州刺史，徙趙郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Nanyang, made Pacifying-South General and Inspector of Jing Province, then enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Nanyang, made pacifying-south general and Jing inspector, then enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宗慶在州，為民所訟，雖訊鞫獲情，上下大不相得。

translations.literal: In the province Zongqing was sued by the people; though inquiry and trial proved the facts, high and low were deeply at odds.
translations.idiomatic: In his province the people brought suit against Zongqing; though investigation proved the charges, he and they were utterly estranged.

sentences.zh: 轉徐州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Xu Province, still holding the same general's title.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Xu inspector while keeping the same army title.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐妻韓巫蠱，伏誅。

translations.literal: Before long, because his wife Han practiced witchcraft, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his wife Han was found guilty of witchcraft and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 宗慶子伯忻，與父俱死。

translations.literal: Zongqing's son Boxin died with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing's son Boxin died with him.

sentences.zh: 伯忻子儼，逃越得免。

translations.literal: Boxin's son Yan fled south and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Boxin's son Yan fled south and survived.

sentences.zh: 後歷尚書郎，除常山太守，轉安南將軍、光祿大夫、持節、兼尚書左丞、郢州行臺，又加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Masters of Writing gentleman, was made Administrator of Changshan, then Pacifying-South General, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, Bearer of the Staff, Acting Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing and Jingzhou Mobile Headquarters, and again Pacifying-Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was a Masters of Writing gentleman, then Changshan administrator, then pacifying-south general, grand master of splendid virtue, bearer of the staff, acting left deputy director of the Masters of Writing and mobile headquarters for Yingzhou, and again pacifying-army general.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮南將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Pacifying-South General and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made pacifying-south general and Jing inspector.

sentences.zh: 穎弟權，從世祖征伐，官至龍驤將軍、豫州刺史，賜爵新野侯。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Quan followed Emperor Shizu on campaigns and reached Dragon-Charging General, Inspector of Yu Province, and the enfeoffment Marquis of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Quan followed Emperor Shizu in war and rose to dragon-charging general, Yu inspector, and Marquis of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，坐法死。

translations.literal: On campaign against the Rouran he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On the Rouran campaign he was executed for a breach of law.

sentences.zh: 弟顥，卒於中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hao died as Attendant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hao died while secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 顥長子靈珍，中書學生、[24]祕書中散。

translations.literal: Hao's eldest son Lingzhen was a Secretariat student and [24] Secretariat Central Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's eldest son Lingzhen was a secretariat student and [24] secretariat central court attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Outer Acting Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made outer acting regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 子羨，歷中書學生、侍御史，以明謹見知。

translations.literal: His son Xian passed through Secretariat student and Attending Censor and was known for clarity and care.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian served as secretariat student and attending censor and was known for sharp judgment and care.

sentences.zh: 出為齊州武昌王征虜長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk on the campaign staff of Prince of Wuchang, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Wuchang's campaign staff as general who campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 後李元護之為齊州，仍為長史，帶東魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Later when Li Yuanhu held Qi Province, Xian remained chief clerk and concurrently Administrator of Eastern Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanhu later held Qi, Xian stayed as chief clerk and concurrently eastern Wei commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 在治十年，經三刺史，以清勤著稱。

translations.literal: In office ten years, through three inspectors, he was famed for pure diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in office under three inspectors, he was famed for clean, tireless service.

sentences.zh: 齊人懷其恩德，號曰良二千石。

translations.literal: The people of Qi cherished his kindness and called him a true two-thousand-dan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi cherished him and called him a true two-thousand-dan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及代還，大受民故送遺，頗以此為損。

translations.literal: When he was replaced and returned, he received many parting gifts from the people — and was somewhat harmed by this.
translations.idiomatic: On his recall he accepted heavy farewell gifts from the people, and his reputation suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 中山王英攻義陽，羨為軍司。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Ying attacked Yiyang; Xian was army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhongshan Ying attacked Yiyang; Xian served as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 罷，除諫議大夫，兼給事黃門侍郎，副侍中游肇為畿內大使。

translations.literal: When it ended he was made Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master and Acting Attendant at the Yellow Gate, assisting Attendant You Zhao as metropolitan envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was made remonstrance and policy grand master and acting attendant at the yellow gate, assisting You Zhao as metropolitan envoy.

sentences.zh: 後行貨於錄尚書、北海王詳，轉大司農少卿。

translations.literal: Later he paid bribes to the Recording Masters of Writing, Prince of Beihai Xiang, and was moved to Vice Minister of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he bribed Recording Masters of Writing Prince of Beihai Xiang and was moved to vice minister of the grand granary.

sentences.zh: 出行荊州事，轉征虜將軍、郢州刺史，鎮義陽。

translations.literal: He conducted affairs of Jing Province, was moved to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Ying Province, and garrisoned Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He handled Jingzhou affairs, then was made general who campaigns against the barbarians and Ying inspector, garrisoning Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 在州銳於聚斂。

translations.literal: In the province he was sharp at levying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he was fierce in levying taxes.

sentences.zh: 又納賄於于忠，徵為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He also paid bribes to Yu Zhong and was summoned as Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also bribed Yu Zhong and was recalled as attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 尋加後將軍、河南尹，黃門如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Rear General and Intendant of Henan, with the yellow gate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made rear general and Henan intendant while keeping the yellow gate post.

sentences.zh: 未拜，而靈太后臨朝，以元昭為河南尹，羨仍黃門，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: Before he took the appointment, Empress Dowager Ling held court; Yuan Zhao was made Intendant of Henan and Xian remained at the yellow gate, with Pacifying-South General added.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Empress Dowager Ling held court; Yuan Zhao was made Henan intendant while Xian stayed at the yellow gate and was given pacifying-south general.

sentences.zh: 羨以義陽軍司之勳，封安陽縣開國子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit as army supervisor at Yiyang, Xian was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyang with an estate of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service as Yiyang army supervisor, Xian was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyang, estate three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 羨曲附左右，故獲封焉。

translations.literal: Xian curried favor with those close to the throne, and therefore received the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xian courted those about the throne, and so won the fief.

sentences.zh: 時幽、瀛、滄、冀大水，頻經寇難，民飢。

translations.literal: At that time You, Ying, Cang, and Ji suffered great floods, repeated raids, and the people were hungry.
translations.idiomatic: You, Ying, Cang, and Ji then suffered great floods, repeated raids, and famine among the people.

sentences.zh: 詔羨兼尚書、假散騎常侍，持節詣州，隨方賑恤，多有所濟。

translations.literal: An edict made Xian Acting Masters of Writing and Acting Regular Attendant, Bearer of the Staff sent to the provinces to relieve according to local need; he aided many.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was made acting Masters of Writing and acting regular attendant, bearer of the staff sent through the provinces to relieve distress where needed, and helped many.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，發疽卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Shengui era an abscess broke out and he died, age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Shengui an abscess broke out and he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 詔賻帛三百匹、朝服一襲，贈鎮東將軍、青州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: An edict granted three hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses and one suit of court dress; posthumously made Pacifying-East General and Inspector of Qing Province, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted three hundred bolts of silk for the funeral and one court robe; posthumously he was made pacifying-east general and Qing inspector, posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子躋，字伯昇，頗有意尚。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ji, styled Bosheng, had considerable aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ji, styled Bosheng, had real ambition.

sentences.zh: 祕書郎。

translations.literal: Secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 朝議以羨本不合山河之賞，故不許躋襲。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that because Xian by origin did not merit a mountains-and-rivers reward, Ji was not allowed to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate held that Xian had not truly earned a territorial fief, so Ji was not allowed to succeed.

sentences.zh: 躋訴訟久之，始聽紹封。

translations.literal: Ji sued and pleaded for a long time before he was at last permitted to receive the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pleaded at law for a long time before succession was finally granted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷前將軍、太中大夫、梁州開府長史。

translations.literal: He was gradually moved to Front General, Grand Master of the Palace, and Chief Clerk of the Liang Province headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to front general, grand master of the palace, and chief clerk of the Liang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 與刺史元羅同陷蕭衍，卒於江南。

translations.literal: With Inspector Yuan Luo he alike fell into Xiao Yan's hands and died in the south.
translations.idiomatic: He and Inspector Yuan Luo alike fell to Xiao Yan and died in the south.

sentences.zh: 子孝緒，元象中，以躋柩還國。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoxu, in the Yuanxiang era, brought Ji's coffin back to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoxu, in the Yuanxiang era, brought Ji's coffin home.

sentences.zh: 興和中，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era he succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent the rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, the rank was reduced by rule.

sentences.zh: 靈珍弟靈奇，立忠將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Lingzhen's younger brother Lingqi was General Who Establishes Loyalty and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen's younger brother Lingqi was general who establishes loyalty and Qi inspector.

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Champion General and he was granted the enfeoffment Marquis of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: His title was raised to champion general and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，有威惠。

translations.literal: His government was pure and simple; he had authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was plain and clean, with both sternness and grace.

sentences.zh: 子恭伯，右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Gongbo was Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongbo was right grand master of splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：為國馭民，莫不文武兼運。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: To steer the state and shepherd the people, none fails to combine civil and military.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: To govern a state and tend its people, none can do without both civil and military craft.

sentences.zh: 燕鳳以博識多聞，昭成致禮，和隣存國，賢之效歟。

translations.literal: Yan Feng, with broad learning and many hearths, won Zhaocheng's courtesy; he harmonized neighbors and preserved the state — is this not the effect of worth?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Feng's wide learning won Emperor Zhaocheng's courtesy; he soothed neighbors and kept the state whole — the work of a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 許謙才術俱美，馳騁艱難之日，觀幾獨勸，事契冥符。

translations.literal: Xu Qian's talent and method were both fine; in galloping through hard days he alone read the moment and urged advance — his cause matched a hidden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian united talent and method; in the hurrying days of crisis he alone saw the hour and urged advance — as if fate itself had marked him.

sentences.zh: 張袞以才策見知，早蒙恩遇，時無寬政，斯言貽咎。

translations.literal: Zhang Gun was known for talent and stratagem, early favored; when the age lacked lenient rule, that saying brought blame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun was prized for talent and counsel and favored early; in an age without gentle government, his words drew reproach.

sentences.zh: 玄伯世家儁偉，仍屬權輿，總機任重，守正成務，禮從清廟，不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: Xuanbo's house was lofty through generations and still stood at the founding; he bore the weight of the pivot, kept to the straight path and finished the work — ritual from the clear temple: was it not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo's clan was great for generations and still stood at the founding; he carried the state's pivot, held the straight course and finished the work — rites worthy of the ancestral temple: could it have been otherwise?

sentences.zh: 寬模俱能見幾而動，道固窮而委質。

translations.literal: Kuan and Mo alike could see the moment and act; when the Way was blocked they still gave their allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuan and Cui Mo alike saw the hour and moved; when the Way was shut they still pledged their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 鄧淵貞白幹事，才業秉筆，禍非其罪，悲哉！

translations.literal: Deng Yuan was upright and white in service, talented in wielding the brush; disaster was not his crime — how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuan was upright in office and skilled with the brush; his fall was not his crime — a bitter loss!

translations.literal: Commentary: "student of the Masters of Writing" appears repeatedly; below on Zi Xian it says "served as student of the Masters of Writing" — shu is supplied now.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "student of the Masters of Writing" is common; the entry on Zi Xian below says "served as student of the Masters of Writing"—shu is restored.
